items.title: fix(hud): a delivery row and a release row fired at whoever the list moved there (#877)
items.body:
An audit for the class of defect behind the `#88` sweep's index-keyed `everMeasured` — an identity that is a position into something that can change between reads.

**Headline: the class is small, well known in this repository, and had exactly two unfixed members — both already named in an issue that closed without them.** No new instance of the `everMeasured` shape exists anywhere else in `tests/`; that is an honest empty result. The two real ones are player-facing, in `src/ui/hud/`.

## The two

`src/ui/hud/build-panel.ts:2318`, `paintDeliveries`:
```ts
      const delivery = shown.deliveries[index];
```
`src/ui/hud/staff-panel.ts:1233`, `paintHeld`:
```ts
      const guard = guards[index];
```

`src/ui/hud/pooled-row-binding.ts:15` states the assumption outright — the "stated assumption is a gift" case:

> `* Every one of those blocks binds `rows[i]` to `items[i]`. A queue advances by`

It names **four** blocks. Two were fixed and gated (Build queue, #860; Staff roster, #877). #877's own closing comment says why the other two were not, verbatim:

> *"`paintHeld` and `paintDeliveries` are **not yet measured** — the pass was cut off by a transient API overload before reaching them."*

**Both re-point with no press from the player**, which makes them worse than the two already fixed rather than milder: a delivery leaves its window by *landing*, on the procurement clock (`PROCUREMENT_DELIVERY_DELAY_TICKS`), and a hold ends when the search or incident response that owns the guard does. **The head of each list is replaced while the player is reading it.** Reading the id at press time does not help — label and id are written in the same synchronous paint, so the id read at press time is exactly the id the row was painted with.

**Fix:** `assignPooledRows` in both, plus `freedAtMs` and a settle constant per list, both aliasing the existing 1,000 ms `BUILD_QUEUE_ROW_SETTLE_MS` rather than inventing a fourth judgement. Each block's "and N more" line is now counted against rows actually **drawn**.

## Mutation evidence

New gate `tests/browser/ui-pooled-rows-aim.spec.ts` — harness-mounted HUD, `page.mouse.click` at a box captured by the same read that captured the label, never a locator.

**A — `paintDeliveries`' `assignPooledRows` replaced by the index binding it displaced:**
```
    Error: the press did not cancel the purchase the row named
    - Expected  - 1
    + Received  + 1
      Array [
    -   "buy-2",
    +   "buy-3",
      ]
```

**B — `paintHeld`'s:**
```
    Error: the press did not release the guard the row named
    - Expected  - 1
    + Received  + 1
      Array [
    -   2,
    +   3,
      ]
```

Restored: `2 passed (6.0s)`. Each mutation reverted from a copy taken beforehand and verified with `sha256sum -c` (`OK` on both files).

### The gate's first run found something about itself, and it is the part worth carrying

With the fixture's totals at 4 → 3, the "and N more" line goes from *"and 1 more"* to hidden across the publication under the index binding; the panel loses a line of `--font-size-eyebrow`, every row moves, and the press at the read coordinate landed back on the purchase it had been aimed at **by accident** — the gate went red on the places array rather than on the command, i.e. **reported the mechanism instead of the harm**. Totals are now 5 → 4 so the overflow line stands in both publications under either binding. The same effect was measured directly on the held-guards block as **21.19 px** of row movement.

**What the gate does not cover, stated rather than implied:** the *second* half of `assignPooledRows`' invariant — a freed place staying blank for `settleMs` — is not exercised for these two lists. The harness publishes once per call and `assignPooledRows` refuses an arrival into a place emptied by the same pass whatever the window is, so a `settleMs` of `0` would still pass this file. Covering it needs a second publication after a real delay.

## A third, low stakes

`tests/browser/playtest-2026-09-04-is-there-anything-to-do.playtest.ts:489` diffed two DOM control censuses three simulated days apart **by position**, so one arriving control reports the whole tail as changed — and the act's whole question is whether three untouched days change the controls. Now keyed on `tag[class] "label"`, arrivals and departures named separately. This is an instrument, not a gate (`testMatch: /.*\.spec\.ts$/`), so it produced a misleading log line, never a false green.

## Safe-but-fragile — correct today, deliberately not fixed

- **`tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts:11985-11986`** — `painted[].prisoner` is a packed `EntityId`; `expectedWindow` holds *positions* into `records.riskTier`, which is by entity index. `packEntityId` puts the index in the low 20 bits and the generation above, so the two coincide **only while every prisoner is at generation 0**. The #703 scenario admits twelve and releases nobody, so they do. Any release falsifies it. It fails **loudly** — a false-red waiting to happen, not a false-green — and the file is PR #1273's right now. Cheapest fix (~4 lines): compare `packEntityId(index, generation)`, or assert the generations are all zero so the premise is pinned rather than inherited.
- **`src/ui/hud/regime-panel.ts:1303`** — the prisoner roster's four pooled rows, index-bound, and the window genuinely re-points (sorted by descending risk tier, so a tier change re-orders it on the simulation's clock). Not fixed for one reason: **the control is not destructive** — it selects a prisoner for the detail block, so the harm is reading about the wrong person, not spending money or ending an employment. The fix is the identical `assignPooledRows` substitution, now applied four times.
- **`tests/foundation/pseudo-locale-contract.test.ts:188`** — pairs `Object.values` against `Object.values` by position while the assertion pinning the two entries compares key lists **sorted**, so a reordering is invisible to it. Measured rather than reasoned: **2 plural entries, 0 order-mismatched**. Safe **for a reason neither the test nor the schema states** — both catalogues go through zod, which rebuilds an object in schema declaration order. One-line durable fix: look the source form up by its plural key.

## Safe, with the reason — these are the patterns worth copying

`tests/foundation/comment-stripping-contract.test.ts:199` is the exemplar: index correspondence with the stability assumption **asserted, not narrated** (`:215`, *"stripping changed a file length, so offsets into the stripped text no longer index the source"*). `composeRenderActorId` is the same class already fixed — two `EntityStore`s both hand out index 0, so the population is folded into the id. And `src/ui/simulation-prisoner-roster.ts:286` refuses the class at the protocol level: *"an offset is not a stable name for a set of people across ticks — 'page 3' would silently be a different three prisoners after a release."*

## How the search ran

Eleven greps, listed in the commit so the next pass can widen rather than repeat. The decisive one for the empty result: `grep -rniE "const (ever|seen|covered|visited|measured|reached|touched|hit|pressed|used)[A-Za-z]* *(: *[A-Za-z<>, ]+)? *= *(new Set|new Map|\[\])"` — ~40 accumulators, **every one keyed by a string id or description except `everMeasured`**. Two separate prose passes with different wording were needed; the second surfaced `canonical-iteration.ts:118` and `ui-shell.spec.ts:1507`, which the first missed.

**What this does not bound** is how many members the greps cannot see. A positional identity in a variable named nothing like an index, or asserted in a sentence worded unlike either prose pass, is invisible by construction — the same limit `docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` §4 records about its own cited-set regex. **A clean result is a statement about what the greps found.**

## Gates

`npx tsc -b` clean. `npx vitest run` — **457 files, 5409 passed, 3 skipped**. Browser: `ui-staff-dismiss` + `build-deliveries-outside-the-fold` + `ui-pooled-rows-aim` **10 passed**; `ui-build-order-note` + `ui-staff-payroll-reachable` + `ui-staff-wage` + `ui-shell` **170 passed**; `app-shell.spec.ts -g "delivery|deliveries|held|release|#285|#703"` **3 passed**. Full browser suite not run.

No player-visible string added or changed. `hud.build.deliveries-more` and `hud.security.held-more` are unchanged, and the commit quotes both beside the reason their **truth** improved: the count they are given is now the rows the player actually cannot reach.

## Weakest claim

That the 1,000 ms settle window is right for these two lists. It is **inherited, not measured** — `BUILD_QUEUE_ROW_SETTLE_MS`' own header calls it *"the weakest number in this design"*, its ~800 ms lower bound was measured on the *queue*, and nobody has measured a decision delay on a delivery row or a release row. What would change it: the measurement #877 asked for and never got, for which `playtest-877-a-dismiss-row-fires-at-who-it-named.playtest.ts` already carries an unrun act on both surfaces.

Refs #877, #860.

items.title: feat(hud): Undo and Redo get a pointer and touch route in the status strip (#1356)
items.body:
Closes #1356. Before this change, Undo and Redo were only reachable through `KeyZ`/`KeyY`, so a touch player had no way to take anything back (`AGENTS.md` boundary 10). This PR adds a pair of icon buttons to the status strip. The strip is present on every tab and at every viewport, phones included.

## Why the strip (Shape 1), not the Build/Rooms panels (Shape 2)

- The key works in the `world` and `construction` contexts on every tab. Shape 2 would only reach two of six tabs, and it would need two copies of the controls whose enabled state could drift apart.
- The player who needs the buttons most is on a phone, and `.hud__corner` is `display: none` there.

Shape 1's cost was measured in the assembled page, against a second worktree of unmodified `4a7215f7`:

| Viewports | Scale | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1280x720, 1280x800, 1440x900, 1024x768, 900x600 | 100 % | No change: same strip height, same visible chips, same Build panel box. The pair takes its 92 px out of the clock group's `flex: 1` stretch. |
| 390x844, 375x812 | 100 % | Strip 103.7 → 128.7 px (+25), same chip count. |
| Desktop viewports | 150 % / 200 % | The strip gets shorter. The cost moves into the counters instead: one to three fewer chips fully visible. |

On phones the pair is positioned absolutely in the strip's top-right corner, next to the Layout button.

Arrangements the browser gates rejected, each recorded in the commit messages:
- Pair on its own row below 720 px: `.save-panel` moved over the centre of the screen and five 200 % combinations went over the ceiling.
- Pair on the counters' row: broke #634.
- Pair beside the brand badge: covered the Layout button.

## What changed

- `src/ui/hud/status-strip.ts`: adds a `.hud-strip__history` group (`role="group"`). It is not inside the transport group and not inside `foldable`.
- `src/ui/hud/hud.ts`: the buttons call `dispatchCommand({ kind: 'undo' | 'redo' }, strip.historyControlFor(...))`.
  - Both buttons join the busy group.
  - A refused press is marked on the button that was pressed.
  - The keyboard path (`attachHistory`) is unchanged. Its docblock sentence "no control on screen" is marked as corrected.
- `src/ui/primitives/icon-button.ts`: the listener now goes through a closure calling `options.onActivate()`, the same way `action-button.ts` does. This lets the reachability walk follow any icon button to its `<button>`.
- `src/ui/primitives/icon.ts`: new `undo` and `redo` glyphs.
- **The buttons are always enabled.** Whether anything is undoable is known only in the worker (`ConstructionSystem.hasSomethingToUndo`), and no such state is sent to the main thread. Pressing on an empty history does what the key does: nothing, silently. Showing a disabled state honestly would need a protocol change; that is left as a follow-up.

## Player-visible strings (authored under the 2026-09-04 release)

| Key | EN | PL |
|---|---|---|
| `hud.history.group-label` | "Undo and redo" | "Cofanie i ponawianie" |
| `hud.history.undo-last-change` | "Undo the last placement" | "Cofnij ostatnie postawienie" |
| `hud.history.redo-last-undone` | "Redo the last undone placement" | "Ponów ostatnie cofnięte postawienie" |

The code that makes these true:
- **"placement":** the undo stack only holds what `ConstructionSystem.registerTransactionOrder` records, and it has exactly two callers:
  - `src/simulation/construction/handler.ts:131` (`PlaceBuildOrder`): `constructionSystem.registerTransactionOrder(order.id, simCommand.transactionId);`
  - `src/simulation/objects/object-placement-service.ts:566` (`PlaceObject`): `this.orders.registerTransactionOrder(request.orderId, request.orderId);`

  So what Undo takes back is always a wall or an object that was placed.
- **Undo:** `undo()` pops the newest transaction. If something else has happened since, ADR 0104's handler refuses and the refusal band gives its own sentence.
- **Redo:** `redo()` pops the newest redo entry. Only `undo()` pushes redo entries, and any new stack write clears them.
- **Wording:** the labels avoid the word "build", because `getByRole('button', { name: 'Build' })` matches substrings in 19 spec uses. `docs/PLAYER_STRINGS.md` was regenerated.

## Contracts and a pinned number that moved

- **Reachability contract:** `NO_CONTROL_ISSUES_IT` is now empty. The count moves 16/2 → 18/0, and `icon-button.ts` joins the list of primitives.
- **Refusal-surface enumeration:** two strip rows added. `docs/IDENTITY_V5_ROLLOUT.md` gets a dated amendment and keeps the old figures.
- **`ARRIVAL_PANEL_HEIGHT_PX['375x812']` moves 447.7 → 429.** This is an exact `toBe` measurement log, not a floor, and it has moved in both directions before. The new entry gives the measured chain: strip 103.7 → 128.7, rail 650.3 → 625.3, aside 162.6 → 156.3, panel 447.7 → 429. So the phone's Rooms panel gives 18.7 px to the only touch route Undo and Redo have. **This is the trade to review.**
- `KNOWN_FAILING` in the 200 % ratchet is unchanged at 12.

## Evidence

**Red before, green after.** Each mutation below was applied and then reverted:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Listener in `icon-button.ts` reverted to a bare reference | Reachability gate: 2 failed, `expected 16 to be 18` |
| Strip `onActivate` unwired | Reachability gate: 2 failed, `expected 17 to be 18` |
| `hud.ts` passing no control for Undo, and Redo dispatching `undo` | All three new browser tests failed |

**Gates:**
- **The agent's full browser run:** 586 passed, 1 failed. It included the #88 sweep at five viewports, #174, #545, #634, the centre-click test and the 200 % ratchet. The one failure is `every runtime atlas reaches the page over HTTP`, which also fails on unmodified `main` in this container because the Git LFS art is not pulled. The `actor-*` and `environment-art` specs fail here for the same reason.
- **Re-run by me on the pushed head `f0b0bbf6`:**
  - `pnpm verify`: typecheck, then 484 files with 5626 passed and 3 skipped, then the production build. Exit 0.
  - The three new #1356 browser tests: `3 passed (10.5s)`.

## Weakest claim

The 18.7 px taken from the phone's Rooms panel. If `ARRIVAL_PANEL_HEIGHT_PX` is meant as a floor rather than a log, the phone arrangement needs a different decision. None of the alternatives measured was free.

items.title: A cancel at the same tick must not make the next order look like a repeat (#861)
items.body:
Closes #861.

## The defect, reproduced headless at #861's own figures

`tests/integration/construction-same-tick-cancel-still-buys.test.ts`, through `Kernel.submitCommand` plus **`dispatchDueCommands()`** rather than `step()` — that is ADR 0051's paused dispatch, and it is what lets the whole run happen at one tick. Two walls, `Cancel` on the second, six more walls: eight presses, tick 0. On `f948b8e2` before the fix:

```
STANDING 7  DEMAND bricks 14  IN FLIGHT 2  SPENT 80
lastReport {"tick":0,"purchased":[],"unfunded":[],"unprocurable":[],"nextOrderShortfallMinorUnits":0}
pendingIds jit:0:item.brick:2
```

Seven standing orders wanting fourteen bricks, **two** on the road, one wall's worth of money spent, and a `lastReport` with an empty `unfunded` — so nothing on the panel said so.

**Why.** A just-in-time purchase id is `jit:<tick>:<itemId>:<inFlightBefore>`, and its docblock argued that `inFlightBefore` is strictly increasing within a tick. A **cancel** at that tick lowers it. Two walls take `…:0` and `…:2`; `Cancel` cancels `…:0` (`largestSurplusDelivery` ties on ascending id), putting the in-flight total back to 2 **without freeing the id that names 2**; every further wall at that tick composes `…:2` again, is refused as `duplicate-order`, and is swallowed.

**One precision correction to the issue as filed:** "nothing purchased at all" is true of the **report** (`purchased: []`, which is what the panel reads) and false of the treasury — 80 had already left earlier in that tick.

**And it is a delay, not a loss — but an unbounded one.** Measured on the unfixed tree: the next scheduled `ConstructionSystem` pass buys the whole shortfall and the queue costs exactly `7 × 80 = 560`. But **the tick is part of the id**, so while the clock stays paused every further pass at tick 0 recomposes the same taken id, including the scheduled pass at tick 0 itself. Both halves are now assertions, so a fix that bought the queue twice fails as loudly as the defect did.

## The change

Nine lines of production code in `src/simulation/economy/just-in-time-materials.ts`. `justInTimePurchaseOrderId` gains an optional `attempt`, and the call site asks a new private `freeJustInTimePurchaseOrderId` for the first id in `<base>`, `<base>/1`, `<base>/2`, … that no **pending** delivery carries. The base is unchanged, so every id that never collided is byte-identical — no save, no `data-delivery` attribute, no pinned string moves. It terminates in at most `pendingDeliveries.length` rounds, and `some` is a membership test, so no iteration order reaches the answer.

**The refusal is narrowed, not removed.** `ProcurementSystem.purchase` is untouched and still refuses an already-pending id, which is the protection for the caller it was written for: the player's **Buy** press, whose `order-${crypto.randomUUID()}` id comes from the command and really can arrive twice. Pinned by a new unit case that asks `ProcurementSystem` directly. What prevents a JIT double-buy is the deficit subtraction (`demand − available − inFlight`), unchanged and separately asserted.

## Three findings worth more than the fix

**1. The order id is not the discriminator, and that was the obvious shape.** `QueuedOrderDemand.orderId` is available at the purchase site, but the collision the existing unit test constructs is **one order colliding with itself** (`oneOrder` is `order-1` throughout): buy at `inFlightBefore` 0, buy at 2, first one cancelled, come back at 2. `jit:<tick>:<itemId>:<orderId>` leaves that untouched, and it is not exotic — an earlier order in the walk claims the in-flight bricks a later pass then finds missing, so the same order legitimately buys the same item twice at one tick. Only a discriminator that is a function of the collision itself answers all of them.

**2. The defect was pinned by a test that asserted it as intended behaviour.** `tests/unit/construction-just-in-time-materials.test.ts` → `describe('the one way a just-in-time purchase id can collide')` asserted `collided.unfunded === []` with the sentence *"nothing is owed: the bricks are on the road under that id"* — against a demand of six bricks with two on the road. Four were owed, and its own last assertion measured them being bought one tick later. That is why the defect survived. Kept at the same figures with its conclusion reversed, both directions marked.

**3. The first draft of this fix would have corrupted the session it repairs.** It used `#` as the separator. A purchase order id is an `identifierSchema` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$/`) in two places that reach a player: `economySectionSchema`'s `procurement.pending[].orderId`, so a `#` id **cannot be saved**, and `CancelMaterialPurchase.orderId`, so it **cannot be cancelled** — refused before the kernel. Found by reading the schema, not by a red test: 388 files and 4,464 tests were green on it, because nothing saved a collided session or cancelled a suffixed delivery. Now `/`, with both gaps turned into gates — the unit file asserts every attempt against `identifierSchema` **itself** rather than a restated character set, with `#` as the negative control, and the integration file puts the collided id through `captureSessionSnapshot`/`restoreSimulationRuntime` and a real `CancelMaterialPurchase`.

## Red-then-green

Both mutations restored from a saved copy and verified with `sha256sum -c`, never `git checkout`:

- **Call site back to `justInTimePurchaseOrderId(...)`**: integration `expected 2 to be 14`; unit `six wanted, two on the road, so four are bought -- now, not next tick`. 2 failed / 29 passed.
- **Separator back to `#`**: the save gate fails with `ZodError: Invalid string: must match pattern /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$/`, and the unit gate fails `jit:7:item.brick:2#1 must be nameable by a command and a save`. The round-trip case identifies the collided delivery as *"not one of the base ids"* rather than by looking for the separator, so it cannot be satisfied by a separator it agrees with.

## Gates

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `tsc -b --pretty false` | exit 0 |
| `tsc -b tsconfig.tools.json --pretty false` | exit 0 |
| `vitest run` | **388 files / 4,466 passed, 1 skipped** (baseline 4,464) |
| `scripts/cloudflare-task.mjs build production` | exit 0 |
| browser: the 13 delivery and pending-delivery specs | **13 passed** — and every `data-delivery` id in those runs is a base id, no suffix anywhere |

Both `tsc` exit statuses read directly, never piped. The browser run and both typechecks were re-verified independently on this branch before this PR was opened, and `identifierSchema`'s regex was read at `src/simulation/protocol/types.ts:52` rather than taken from the report.

## No decision taken

No player-facing string changed — the delivery row's label is quantity, material and total; the id only reaches `data-delivery` and `dataset`. No save-schema field, no version bump, no ADR: the id composition was a docblock decision, and every property it documents (deterministic, state-derived, no counter, no clock, no UUID) is preserved.

**Handover, not blocking:** `docs/research/2026-08-30-playing-into-the-lock.md` describes the id as composed "out of a tick, an item and an in-flight total". Still a valid call and still true of a non-colliding purchase, now incomplete. Left alone as a dated research record.

items.title: Close the five decision-free findings the #89 re-check turned up
items.body:
Refs #89, #249, #250. Five findings from the #89 re-check that need no product or architectural decision. The one that does — a purchase surface — is untouched and recorded on #89.

## What the re-check established, for context

The store link **is** closed: `new-session.ts` wires `ProcurementSystem`'s destination and `ContainerMaterialsProvider`'s source from the same local `Container`, and diverting one of them fails two cases of `tests/integration/economy-build-loop.test.ts`. Object identity survives a restore too, because `ContainerRegistry.loadSnapshot` mutates in place.

The chain is broken one link earlier: **nothing in `src/` can issue a `PurchaseMaterials` command.** That is #89's remaining cause, it is a product decision, and this PR does not pre-empt it.

---

## 1. A validation gap between two boundaries that were meant to agree

`purchaseMaterialsSchema` typed `orderId` and `itemId` as `z.string()`. `save-schema.ts`'s `economySectionSchema` requires `identifierSchema` — `min(1).max(128).regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$/)` — of the same two values on a pending delivery, and `createSaveEnvelope` parses and **throws**.

So this sequence was reachable, and verified by execution before the fix:

1. `packCommand({ type: 'PurchaseMaterials', orderId: '_bad id', … })` succeeds.
2. `unpackCommand` returns it intact; the kernel dispatches it.
3. The delivery enters the procurement queue.
4. The next save attempt throws:
   ```
   "code": "invalid_format", "format": "regex",
   "path": ["simulation","economy","procurement","pending",0,"orderId"]
   ```
5. Once the delivery arrives and leaves the queue, saving works again.

An intermittent unreproducible save failure, on a path with no visible connection to its cause. Both fields are `identifierSchema` now, so the id never reaches the queue — the only place a fix can put the failure next to its cause.

**It costs no existing save.** Nothing in `src/` mints a purchase command at all, and a session that had accepted a loose id could not have been saved anyway.

**`PlaceBuildOrder.orderId` is deliberately left as `z.string()`.** Its save-side counterpart (`buildOrderSchema`) is `z.string().min(1)`, which is *looser* than the command schema rather than stricter — so there is no disagreement there to close, and tightening it would be a change with no defect behind it.

## 2. Its `quantity` bound could not fail

Replacing `quantity: z.number().int().positive().max(MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY)` with a bare `z.number()` left **1,666 tests passing**. `PurchaseMaterials` appeared in exactly one test file — an integration test that packs `quantity: 2` — and nothing anywhere asserted the decoder refusing a malformed one. The schema's own comment argues the decode-side bound is not redundant with the system's; that claim was unproven.

`tests/unit/protocol-commands-purchase.test.ts` pins it at **`unpackCommand`**, not `packCommand`. `packCommand` calls `.parse` and throws, so its type signature already refuses most of this at compile time. `unpackCommand` is where a payload from *outside* the process arrives: a restored save's pending queue carries its command payload as opaque JSON (`queuedCommandSchema` types it as `detachedJsonValueSchema`), so a queued command is re-decoded through this schema and through nothing else. `null` — not a throw — is the contract there.

Eight cases: the positive control first (so a schema that rejected everything would not pass), then non-positive and non-integer quantities, both sides of `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY`, the id shapes `identifierSchema` refuses, the id shapes `src/main.ts` actually mints, the dotted catalog id shape that has to keep working, an unknown extra field, and each field omitted.

## 3. A comment that claimed the opposite of what the code does

`ProcurementSystem.order = 110` was justified as:

> After construction (100), so a delivery that lands on a tick construction also runs is visible to that same tick's allocation attempt rather than the next one.

`Kernel.register` sorts **ascending** (`kernel.ts:113`, `a.order - b.order`) and iterates in that order, so 110 runs *later* than construction's 100. Construction is also on `intervalTicks: 10` against procurement's `1`.

**Measured:** a delivery arriving on tick 100 leaves `materials-pending` on tick **110**. The same-tick property never held, in exactly the case the comment describes.

The comment is corrected; the value is not changed. Making the property real means moving below 100, and declared order is part of ADR 0020's determinism contract and ADR 0009's replay guarantee over stored saves — `order = 90` fails `tests/determinism/kernel-system-order.test.ts` by design, which is the gate working. So that is a deliberate reviewed edit with the pin updated in the same change, and the ≤10-tick lag is accepted and now written down.

## 4. The no-teleport rule had gained a second exception in silence

`docs/OPERATIONS.md` said `ContainerMaterialsProvider` "is the one deliberate exception" to every item moving only through a `CarryItemJob`'s two navigation-backed legs. `ProcurementSystem.update` has been calling `deposit` at **no tile at all** since the economy landed.

The section now names both, says why a purchase is not a transfer — there is no source container; the goods are bought from outside the prison and materialise on arrival — and states plainly what is still missing: the physical route through `room.delivery-bay` that ADR 0017 §4 names, without which the deposit is scaffolding and consumption is location-blind (a wall 400 tiles away spends the same global stock as one next door).

Also corrected while there: the same file still showed `ConstructionMaterialsProvider` with only `tryAllocate`, when `release` has been a required member since #97.

`docs/PERSISTENCE.md` had **no mention of the economy at all** — not in the payload map, not in the "what is persisted, and why" table. Both now carry it, with the reason the section is optional.

**And a gate, because deleting that whole section used to leave the suite green.** A new claim in `documentation-claims-contract.test.ts` requires every module outside `src/simulation/operations/` that calls `.deposit(` to be named in the no-teleport section. Shaped as "the document names it" rather than as an allow-list on purpose: an allow-list lets prose and code drift while both look checked, whereas requiring the module's own filename in the section means the only way to add a third exception is to write the paragraph explaining it.

## 5. The gate that would have caught the real defect at declaration time

`tests/foundation/unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts`, modelled on `unconsumed-action-contract.test.ts` and inheriting its argument one level up. That gate exists because five declared input actions were bound to keys and read by nobody; its header says *"A dead key is worse than a missing one — it is indistinguishable from a broken build."* A command the game cannot send is the same object.

**Six commands are declared. One has a producer.**

| Command | Producer |
| --- | --- |
| `PlaceBuildOrder` | `src/main.ts` |
| `CancelBuildOrder` | none |
| `ZoneRoom` | none |
| `PurchaseMaterials` | none |
| `Undo` | none |
| `Redo` | none |

`HudIntent` has five members and not one is a cancel, a zone, a purchase or an undo. Each unproduced command carries a written reason that fails as stale the moment it gains a producer.

Two design points worth stating:

- **The type list comes out of `simulationCommandSchema.options`**, so a seventh member is in scope the moment it is added. A hand-written array here would be a second list to forget, which is the failure this family of gates exists to prevent.
- **A producer is `type: 'X'`, not the bare literal.** A consumer writes `case 'X':` (`construction/handler.ts`) or `command.type === 'X'`. Matching the bare name would count all six handler branches as producers and report the exact opposite of the truth — so there is a dedicated control asserting that `handler.ts` contains `case 'Undo':` and that `producersOf('Undo')` is still empty.

Two limits are stated rather than left to be discovered: a producer assembling the object from a variable is invisible to a text scan, and the scan cannot tell a live dispatch from dead code inside `src/`. Both err toward reporting a command as *produced*, so the failures it raises are real ones.

## Mutations run

Each applied, run, reverted; `git diff --stat` checked non-empty before believing each result.

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `quantity` bound back to `z.number()` | **2 of 8 fail** (was 0 of 1,666) |
| `orderId`/`itemId` back to `z.string()` | **2 of 8 fail** |
| `src/main.ts` stops writing the `PlaceBuildOrder` literal | **3 of 6 fail** |
| A 7th command joins the union with no producer and no entry | **3 of 6 fail**, naming `SetPolicy` in the message |
| The whole no-teleport section deleted | **1 of 10 fails** |
| Section restored to its old singular text, procurement unnamed | **1 of 10 fails**, naming the file |

The last one is the important one: it reproduces the exact pre-existing state and the gate fails with the right diagnosis rather than a generic one.

## Verification

Run in a **clean clone** rather than the working checkout, because concurrent investigation threads had live mutations in `src/simulation/entity/entity-store.ts` and `src/simulation/prisoners/intake-system.ts` at the time and a shared-tree result would have been unattributable.

- `npx tsc -b --pretty false` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — **164 files, 1682 passed, 1 skipped** (was 162 / 1667)
- `npx vite build` — production output written

## What this does not do

**A player still cannot spend the treasury.** #89 stays open, with its cause re-scoped: no longer "nothing can supply materials", now "nothing can ask for materials to be supplied". The buy surface is a product decision — a procurement panel, a quantity stepper on the Build panel, or auto-purchase on order placement — and the refusal route it needs does not exist either.

**ADR 0017 still reads `Proposed — pending human approval. Not accepted.`** and says in terms that nothing in it licenses shipping an economy, while #249's economy is on `main`. And `docs/adr/` has no `0018` because open PR #91 claims that number for a *competing* answer to #89. Both are recorded on #89 for the owner; neither is decided here.

items.title: Give the build queue a surface, and CancelBuildOrder its last missing producer
items.body:
Closes the last gap in `tests/foundation/unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts`:
`CancelBuildOrder` was the repository's **only command with no production
producer**, and the count at the foot of that file moves from *ten produced and
one unproduced* to **eleven produced and none unproduced**. Its
`AWAITING_PRODUCER` list is empty for the first time.

## The gap was a read model, not a button

The entry's reason was correct for as long as it stood. `CancelBuildOrder` takes
an `orderId`, and **no order id reached the main thread at all** —
`src/simulation/protocol/commands.ts` said so where it argues that `RemoveObject`
carries a tile instead: an order id is something *"nothing on screen shows and no
snapshot carries"*. A "cancel" that could not name an order would have been a
second, worse `Undo`.

What changed is **#348**. Construction builds one order at a time, so
`tests/unit/construction-geometry.test.ts`'s twelve-segment run finishes at tick
**730** where it used to finish at **70**, and eleven of those twelve segments now
wait hundreds of ticks — with nothing on screen saying a queue existed at all.

So this is two things: a read model (`hud/build-queue`) that carries the pending
orders and their ids, and a Build-panel block that names each one and can withdraw
it. [ADR 0030](docs/adr/0030-build-queue-cancellation-surface.md) is `Proposed`
with its `STATUS-QUEUE.md` entry in the same commit.

## Two premises in the brief did not survive the code

- **The gate pins ten produced and one unproduced, not nine and one.** Eleven
  commands are declared; `PlaceObject`/`RemoveObject` had already moved it.
- **"You should not need to change `src/simulation/construction/**`"** held, and
  the brief's implied scope did not: the Build panel could not be the whole of it,
  because nothing carried an order id out of the worker. The change is a
  projection, a reader, the view model, the panel and one dispatch.

## The defect this found on the way

The block's cost was first measured through `tests/browser/ui-harness.html` — and
that harness leaves `hud.asideSlot` empty, so `.hud__aside:empty { display: none }`
fires and the Build panel gets **128.7px more rail than the application ever
gives it**. On the assembled page a queue with the block *collapsed* put the panel
15px over its box at 1280x720 and 37px over at 900x600, with the block's own
header **14px and 37px below the panel's unscrolled fold**. Nothing had scrolled.
That is #174 for a third time and this time on a control.

`.hud-build[data-queued]` pays for the 45px out of the one block `hud.css`
designates as shrinkable: `--hud-build-catalogue-floor` drops from two rows to one
*while a queue exists*. It is a floor, so it donates nothing where nothing is
needed. Re-measured assembled with six queued: the panel does not scroll and the
header is above the fold at all five viewports, and the list absorbs
111/0/75/132/66px — the 0 is 1440x900, where both catalogue rows stay. This is
deliberately against that token's own argument for two rows; ADR 0030 decision 3
makes the case and its open question 4 states what refusing it would mean.

## What the surface is

- **`hidden` until something is queued** (the arrival state, so the panel's
  arrival height does not move), **collapsed when it appears** (a 45px header, not
  a list), and opening `scrollIntoView`s the rows exactly as the buy row does.
- **Three rows, pooled.** `BUILD_QUEUE_ROW_LIMIT` carries the height measurement
  *and* the argument: since #348 the list is the crew's schedule, so its head is
  where the decisions are, and `Undo` is still the control for a whole run.
  `hud.build.queue-more` says so to the player. Pooling also keeps the HUD's busy
  group — `add` with no `remove` — from growing over a session, and each cancel
  reads its order id **at press time**.
- **Each row says what, where, which edge and what it is waiting for.** The state
  words come from the `build-order-state` group that already existed and that
  nothing rendered; `assigned` moves from "Assigned" to "Awaiting the Crew",
  because an `assigned` order has its materials and is waiting for the crew, and
  since #348 that is the state a queue of eleven walls spends its whole wait in.
- **No pre-check on the main thread.** Whether an order still exists is the
  simulation's to decide, and it is idempotent about it.

## Proving it

**Assertions that would have been satisfied by the defect were not written.**
Every browser assertion here is a `getBoundingClientRect` or an `offsetParent`,
never `toContainText` — #220's lesson, applied to a control rather than a message.

- `tests/unit/construction-build-queue-projection.test.ts` — the aiming tests over
  a real kernel: three orders, the **middle** one cancelled by id, and the
  assertion is about the two that were not; plus a cancellation of the **oldest**
  order followed by an `Undo` that demonstrably takes a different one.
- `tests/browser/ui-build-queue.spec.ts` (9 tests) — no box until something is
  queued at six viewports; 78x44 cancels with an `offsetParent`, inside the panel
  and inside the viewport at 375x812; the pressed row's id in the dispatched
  intent and no `undo` beside it; a pooled row re-aimed at the order in it now.
- `tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts`'s #88 sweep — it reported all four new
  controls as *"never laid out in any state"*, correctly, because no state it
  visited had a queue. It now builds one through the real application (six orders
  through the panel's numeric route, clock started so they dispatch and stopped so
  they stay) and opens the fold as a fourth panel state beside the buy row.

## Red-proofing

Each production half reverted, the failure quoted, the revert undone. Seven
mutations; **one came back green and that is the most useful line here.**

**1. The projection stops filtering to pending orders**

```
 FAIL  tests/unit/construction-build-queue-projection.test.ts > drops an order once it is
       built, and an order the world refused, so the queue is only what is still coming
AssertionError: expected [ 'order-a', 'order-z' ] to deeply equal [ 'order-a' ]
```

**2. The projection stops ordering by id — green, and the test was wrong**

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 11 skipped (12)
```

The test that claimed to cover it submits three orders backwards and asserts they
come back in ascending id. It cannot see the sort, because
`ConstructionSystem.allOrders()` already returns ascending id — so the source hands
the projection exactly what the projection was going to produce. Its comment said
*"an implementation that passed the source's order straight through would fail"*,
and that sentence was false.

Fixed in `0116d27` with a second test that drives `projectBuildQueue` through its
narrow `BuildOrderSource` with the rows scrambled, asserting each row's tile
travelled with its id — a sort that reordered ids and left tiles behind would pass
on ids alone and aim every cancel at the wrong wall. Re-proofed:

```
 FAIL  ... > sorts what it is handed, so a source that stopped ordering cannot
             silently reorder the panel
AssertionError: expected [ 'order-c', 'order-a', 'order-b' ]
                to deeply equal [ 'order-a', 'order-b', 'order-c' ]
```

**3. `src/main.ts` stops producing the command**

```
 FAIL  tests/foundation/unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts   (4 of 6 assertions)
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'src/main.ts' ]
AssertionError: a declared command type nothing in src/ outside src/simulation/protocol/
                constructs … expected [ 'CancelBuildOrder' ] to deeply equal []
AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0
```

**4. The reader stops carrying order ids through**

```
 FAIL  tests/unit/ui-simulation-build-queue.test.ts   (5 assertions)
AssertionError: expected [ 'order-01', 'order-01', 'order-01' ]
                to deeply equal [ 'order-01', 'order-02', 'order-03' ]
```

**5. The panel stops hiding the block for an empty queue**

```
 FAIL  tests/browser/ui-build-queue.spec.ts > has no box at all until something is
       queued, at every viewport
Error: the queue block has a box before anything asked at 1440x900
```

**6. A row's cancel names the first order instead of its own — the aiming claim**

```
 FAIL  tests/browser/ui-build-queue.spec.ts > cancels the order that was pressed and
       leaves the other rows alone
- "{\"kind\":\"cancel-build-order\",\"orderId\":\"order-01\"}"
+ "{\"kind\":\"cancel-build-order\",\"orderId\":\"order-00\"}"
```

The second row was pressed and the first order was cancelled. That is exactly the
"cancels the current one" control this surface exists not to be.

**7. The catalogue stops paying for the block's 45px**

```
 FAIL  tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts > every control can actually be pressed, on every
       tab and at every viewport (#88)
Error: the Build panel scrolls on arrival at 1280x720
Expected: false   Received: true
```

## Housekeeping

- Three assertions in `app-shell.spec.ts` reached the numeric fallback's header as
  "the panel's last `.ui-section`" and timed out clicking an invisible one. That
  section is named now (`.hud-build__coordinates`) and its `.ui-action` lookups are
  scoped with it, because a bare `.ui-section__body .ui-action` matches every
  cancel in the queue. The #174 fold assertion **gains** a second half rather than
  losing its first.
- `commands.ts`'s argument for `RemoveObject` taking a tile loses half its premise
  and keeps its conclusion, and says so.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` and `docs/TESTING.md` are
  corrected: two readers on the projection channel, thirteen projection ids, and
  `TESTING.md`'s "painted by nothing yet" — already stale before this change — is
  fixed.

## Suite status

**CI is green on `0116d27`: `verify` success, `assets` success, `browser` success.**

Locally, `pnpm verify` is clean (212 files, 2412 tests) and the browser suite is
173 passed / 1 failed — `every runtime atlas reaches the page over HTTP and decodes
at its authored size`, which is environmental and pre-existing here:
`public/assets/actors/*.png` are git-lfs pointer files in this checkout rather than
PNGs. It passes on the runner, which has the objects.

CI at the intermediate commit `77328e4` reported two failures and both are settled.
One was the stale assertion this branch then fixed in `922769f`. The other was
`a world press with nothing to remove says so at 375x812` timing out for 15s on
*"the simulation never advanced"* — a clock-startup wait unrelated to this change
(that test starts on the Overview tab, where the queue reader is inert). It passed
locally on the same tree and passes on CI now.

items.title: [Construction] No surface can issue a `PurchaseMaterials` command, so a build order still cannot complete
items.body:
> **Correction — 2026-08-24.** Re-verified line by line against `main` at `9b6965a` (v0.0.16). **The symptom still reproduces; the stated cause no longer holds, and three supporting claims are refuted.** #249 and #250 closed the *last* link of the supply chain — a purchase now deposits into the very `Container` that `ConstructionSystem` draws from — so the chain breaks one link earlier, at the player's end. The title and the "Why" section are rewritten to the link that is actually missing; the three refuted claims are deleted rather than left to mislead, each named below with what is true in its place. Everything else is as filed.
>
> Deleted, with the correction:
> - *"`BUILDABLE_REGISTRY` requires item ids `brick` / `wood-plank`; `src/content/item-catalog.ts` declares `item.brick` / `item.wood-plank`. Two vocabularies that have never met…"* — **fixed in #97.** `src/simulation/construction/definition.ts:24` reads `materialsRequired: [{ itemId: 'item.brick', quantity: 2 }]`, and `:45-46` records the old split in the past tense.
> - *"`ConstructionSystem.cancelOrder` carries a `// TODO: release materials`."* — **implemented.** `src/simulation/construction/system.ts:246` is `this.materialsProvider.release(order.materialsAllocated);`. The only surviving occurrence of that TODO string is inside a comment at `src/simulation/construction/materials-provider.ts:17` describing the former state.
> - *"There is no money in this repository and none should be introduced here."* — **refuted by #249.** `src/simulation/economy/` ships `treasury.ts` and `procurement.ts`, and #250 put the treasury balance on the HUD status strip.
>
> **State note, for the owner rather than acted on here:** this issue is currently *closed* (by PR #262, the documentation sweep), while on that same commit `tests/foundation/unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts:90-91` still records `PurchaseMaterials` as *"#89, unchanged in symptom and changed in cause"*.

## What happens

Place a build order in a real session — through the HUD build panel, `WorkerStateMachine`'s `simulation/initialize` `{kind: 'new'}` path, or `InProcessSessionHost.startNew` — and it reaches `materials-pending` and stays there forever. No wall is ever built, no geometry is ever written, no room is ever enclosed. The core loop cannot complete.

## Why — the link that is actually missing

**Nothing in `src/` can construct a `PurchaseMaterials` command.**

```
$ grep -rn "type: 'PurchaseMaterials'" src/ tests/
tests/integration/economy-build-loop.test.ts:94
tests/unit/protocol-commands-purchase.test.ts:44
```

Two hits, both tests. `HudIntent` (`src/ui/hud/hud.ts:128`) has five members — `select-tab`, `set-clock`, `toggle-panel`, `place-build-order`, `arm-build-tool` — and none of them is a purchase. The command is declared, schema-bounded and handled; it is reachable only from the suite.

Compounding it: #250 put the treasury balance on the status strip, so a player now *sees* money they cannot spend.

## Why the original cause no longer applies

The original diagnosis was that nothing ever deposits into the construction-materials container and *"there is no route by which materials enter a prison"*. There is one now, and it is wired by default:

- `src/simulation/runtime/new-session.ts:193-195` registers the `Container` under `CONSTRUCTION_MATERIALS_CONTAINER_ID` and wires a `ContainerMaterialsProvider` over it into `ConstructionSystem`.
- `:208` constructs `new ProcurementSystem(treasury, constructionMaterials)` — passing **that same container object** as the delivery destination.
- `src/simulation/economy/procurement.ts:167` is `this.destination.deposit(delivery.itemId, delivery.quantity);`.

So a purchase spends now and delivers later into exactly the store construction draws from, and object identity survives a snapshot restore. What is missing is the player's ability to make the purchase at all.

`ConstructionSystem.update` still calls `materialsProvider.tryAllocate(def.materialsRequired)` on every scheduled tick while an order is `materials-pending`, and against a container nothing can fill, that returns `false` forever — the same observable end state, one link further up.

## The decided fix

**A quantity stepper on the Build panel.** Recorded by the owner in ADR 0017 (`docs/adr/0017-money-primary-resource-model.md:161`: *"The owner has decided the surface: a quantity stepper on the Build panel."*). The remaining open half is whether a refused purchase is reported to the player.

⚠️ **Warning for whoever implements it.** `tests/foundation/unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts` holds a `PurchaseMaterials` entry in `AWAITING_PRODUCER` (`:90-91`). That gate fails as **stale** the moment the command gains a producer — `:179-180`, *"these commands now have a producer in `src/`: delete their `AWAITING_PRODUCER` entries in the same change"*. **The entry must be deleted in the same change that adds the stepper**, not in a follow-up.

## Not in scope

Deliveries, shipments and any renewable supply need something able to refuse them, which is #29's economy — the slice of it that exists is `src/simulation/economy/`, and the ledger, grants and recurring costs remain #29's.

items.title: [Economy] Give a paid-for delivery a way back, beside the control that bought it (#285)
items.body:
Closes #285 on the decision recorded there: **resolution 2 — a purchase-cancel command with its own surface.**

`ProcurementSystem.cancel` refunds the *recorded* `paidMinorUnits` of a delivery that has not landed, exactly. It is idempotent, snapshotted, restored and tested — and `grep -rn "procurement\.cancel" src/` found nothing, so the only caller in the repository was `tests/integration/economy-build-loop.test.ts:238`. It is one of only two things in the simulation that credit the treasury, and **no session a player could drive could produce it**: money spent on a delivery they had changed their mind about was unrecoverable, with no affordance explaining it and none recovering it.

The blocker was the one `CancelBuildOrder` had before #367, one system over. A purchase `orderId` is minted on the main thread by the press that spends the money and then forgotten, so a command could not usefully have named one. **What was missing was a read model, not a button.**

Every measured claim in #285's decision comment reproduced on `origin/main` before building on it: `cancel` refunds the record rather than recomputing, `pendingDeliveries` is a public accessor, `snapshot`/`restore` carry the pending list, and `AWAITING_PRODUCER` was empty.

---

## What lands

| piece | file |
| --- | --- |
| `CancelMaterialPurchase { orderId }` — schema, `commandJson`, union | `src/simulation/protocol/commands.ts` |
| the branch that routes it to `ProcurementSystem.cancel` | `src/simulation/runtime/session-commands.ts` |
| `hud/pending-deliveries` over `projectPendingDeliveries` | `src/simulation/presentation/procurement-projection.ts`, `worker/projection-catalog.ts` |
| the reader — fourth painter of #104's channel | `src/ui/simulation-pending-deliveries.ts` |
| the surface: pending deliveries **inside the buy disclosure** | `src/ui/hud/build-panel.ts`, `hud.css` |
| the intent, the dispatch, the cadence | `src/ui/hud/hud.ts`, `src/main.ts` |

`cancel` now answers a `PurchaseCancelOutcome` instead of a boolean, so a cancellation with nothing left to refund is a **reported** refusal (`cancel-purchase.not-pending`, a ninth wire namespace) rather than a silent no-op. That is the one signature change, and it is what lets the handler tell the player the money did not come back.

**No persisted shape moves and no save version.** `pendingDeliveries` is already a public accessor over the list `snapshot`/`restore` carry and `economySectionSchema` already types every field — this reads state a V5 save has held all along, so **V6 stays free** for #361 and #337. `src/persistence/save-schema.ts` is untouched.

---

## Where the surface went, and the measurement that justifies it

**Not a third block in the Build panel.** The catalogue is the only block `hud.css` lets that panel take height from; ADR 0031 decision 3 already spends 45px of it on the queue block, and with twenty-one buildables that leaves the list a **44px box over 924px of rows** at 900x600 — one row of twenty-one — which is exactly what that ADR's open question 4 asks about. A block appearing whenever a delivery was pending would have been a second donation out of the same donor.

So the rows live **inside the buy disclosure**, which has no box until the player opens it. A pending delivery is a *purchase*, not a build order: the id it carries was minted by the press two controls above it, and the money it refunds is the money that press spent.

### 900x600, assembled page, Build tab, one prison, coordinates folded

**Before / after, arrival state** — five purchases outstanding, disclosure closed, against the same page with nothing bought:

| | nothing bought | five purchases out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| panel height | 338.1px | **338.1px** |
| body content / box | 291.2 / 291.2px | **291.2 / 291.2px** |
| panel overflow | 0 | **0** |
| catalogue list box / content | 88 / 924px | **88 / 924px** |
| "Enter coordinates" inside the fold by | 7.8px | **7.8px** |

Identical to the tenth of a pixel, at all five viewports the suite visits. The catalogue donates nothing and no token moves.

**Opened** (the state the player asked for, which this panel already scrolls in — `paintBuy`, and ADR 0031 decision 3's third case):

| pending | buy row | panel overflow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | 128.4px | 125px |
| one | 199.7px | 196px |
| three + the "and N more" line | **312.9px** | 309px |

The panel's visible box is **337.0px**, so the whole open row fits: after the disclosure's own `scrollIntoView` the panel sits at `scrollTop` 260, every Cancel is 78x44, inside the box, and hit-tests to itself.

**Four rows does not fit, and that is why the limit is three.** With the limit mutated to 4 and five purchases out, the row is **360.9px** and the fourth Cancel measures:

```
{"hasOffsetParent": true, "height": 44, "width": 78, "hitsItself": true, "insidePanel": false}
```

Laid out, a full tap target, hit-testable — and 7.9px below the panel's visible bottom. That is #220's exact shape, and the app-shell test goes red on it.

**Stated cost.** While the buy toggle is hidden (removal mode, or a buildable nothing sells) the disclosure cannot be opened and these rows are unreachable. Hiding the toggle in removal mode is load-bearing — it is what gives the third button in `.hud-build__actions` its room back on a row ADR 0022 measured a third control overflowing by 37.9px — so the alternative was re-opening a measured overflow. It is one tap out of removal mode, and it is written next to the code.

---

## The headline guarantee, in exact minor units

`tests/integration/economy-purchase-cancellation.test.ts`, driven through `createNewSimulationRuntime` + `Kernel.step()` with the real `packCommand`:

```
session start                          balance=25000
PurchaseMaterials 3 × item.brick @40    balance=24880   pending=1
CancelMaterialPurchase                  balance=25000   pending=0   refusals=0
300 ticks later (nothing arrives)       balance=25000   bricks=0
```

and the aiming case, three deliveries of 1/2/4 bricks with the middle one cancelled:

```
three purchases                         balance=24720
CancelMaterialPurchase buy-b            balance=24800   pending=[buy-a, buy-c]
after both arrive                       balance=24800   bricks=5
```

and #285's mutation M1 from the other side — a delivery that has already landed:

```
purchased, delivered                    balance=24920   bricks=2
CancelMaterialPurchase                  balance=24920   bricks=2
                                        refusal=cancel-purchase.not-pending  count=1
```

On the assembled page, `app-shell.spec.ts` presses a real Cancel and polls the Funds readout back **up** by exactly one delivery's price.

---

## Tests: watched red first

Every new test was run against the unfixed tree (production changes stashed, the two new `src/` files moved aside) before being run green.

**Red on `origin/main`'s code, with the new tests present:**

```
tests/unit/procurement-pending-deliveries-projection.test.ts   6 tests | 6 failed
tests/integration/economy-purchase-cancellation.test.ts        6 tests | 6 failed  (ZodError: unknown command type)
tests/unit/ui-simulation-pending-deliveries.test.ts            suite failed to import
tests/unit/ui-hud-build-panel.test.ts                         28 tests | 5 failed
tests/integration/economy-build-loop.test.ts                   5 tests | 1 failed
tests/browser/ui-pending-deliveries.spec.ts                   11 tests | 8 failed
tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts -g "pending delivery costs"     1 failed
foundation/unit gates (command count, refusal vocabulary,
  orchestration manifest, ui module list, painter list)         9 failed
```

Two of the three browser tests that passed against the unfixed tree passed *vacuously* — they assert that nothing is drawn — so each gained a non-vacuity tail. With those, they go red too (`a non-empty list drew nothing at 1440x900`, `the block is not drawn when opened at 1440x900`).

**Green after:**

```
pnpm verify         227 files, 2,560 tests, production build clean
pnpm test:browser   187 passed, 1 failed
```

The one browser failure is the Git-LFS-pointer atlas decode (`actor.cook.base.idle.png did not decode at its authored size`), which fails in this container by design; `pnpm verify:assets` likewise. Baseline on `origin/main` was 224 files / 2,534 tests.

**Sensitivity, by mutation on the fixed code** — no assertion in this change is satisfied by construction:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| projection sorts by `orderId` alone (the build queue's rule) | 2 red |
| `refundableMinorUnits` summed over the window instead of the list | 1 red |
| `cancel` answers `ok` for an id it never held | 3 red |
| `PENDING_DELIVERY_ROW_LIMIT` 3 → 4 | app-shell red, naming the off-screen control |

No fixture computes its expected value from the code under test: prices and balances are literals, the two constants they rest on (`TREASURY_STARTING_BALANCE_MINOR_UNITS` 25,000 and `item.brick` 40) are pinned once so a content change fails with the arithmetic named, the row count is asserted as a literal `3` rather than as the constant being guarded, and the projection's ordering is driven from a hand-built out-of-order source because `purchase` and `restore` both sort.

---

## Gates and documentation

- `unconsumed-command-contract` moves to **twelve produced, none unproduced**. `AWAITING_PRODUCER` stays empty: the twelfth command arrived with its producer, its consumer and its read model in one change.
- `simulation-refusals` gains a ninth namespace, `cancel-purchase.*`, kept apart from `purchase.*` for the reason `unzone` is kept apart from `zone`: buying and un-buying are opposite gestures on one treasury, and somebody who pressed Cancel must not read that the materials were not ordered.
- `projection-reachability-contract` gains a fourth painter; `PROJECTION_IDS` moves to fourteen.
- The `#88` sweep needed a third setup state. Its `neverLaidOut` gate correctly failed and named all three new Cancel buttons, so the setup now buys three deliveries the same way it queues six orders — through the real controls, with the clock started and then paused.
- **`docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` gap 21 is corrected**, which #285 predicted would be needed: it said the refund had no surface and named the decision as open, and both halves are now false. Section 9 gains the reader and the count; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s reader list moves with it.

---

## Two things worth a reviewer's attention

**1. ADR 0031's acceptance is not on `main`.** The decision comment gates this work on 0031's approval, and the approving commit (`1012e2b`) is on the unmerged branch `docs/accept-adr-0031-0032`. On `origin/main` — which this branch is cut from — the ADR's Status still reads `Proposed`, so `adr-status-reference-contract.test.ts` correctly rejected prose here that called it accepted. The code therefore cites the ADR's **content** (decision 3, open question 4) and its arithmetic, never its status. The acceptance's condition is respected on the merits: this surface takes nothing from the catalogue.

**2. Nothing in the code contradicted the decision's reasoning.** Every measured claim in it held. One thing it did not anticipate: `ProcurementSystem.cancel` returning a boolean is not enough to satisfy the repository's own refusal rules — `simulation-refusals.test.ts` requires each wire reason to come from an exhaustive `Record` over a named union — so making the refusal reportable, rather than a silent no-op, required the outcome type. That is the one production signature this change moves, and it is the change that keeps a Cancel from appearing to refund money it did not.

Open question 4 of ADR 0031 stays open: this change does not take the catalogue's remaining row, and does not give it the surface of its own that its acceptance asks for.

items.title: A queue row cancels what it named (#860) — and both fixes I proposed were refuted by measurement
items.body:
Closes #860.

## Reproduced, three times, with the press a player actually makes

`page.mouse.click` at the button box read alongside the label — **not** a locator, because a locator re-resolves `[data-order]` and a player has no selector. Against `main`:

| delay before the press | wrong order cancelled |
|---|---|
| 0 ms | 0 of 1 |
| 250 ms | 1 of 1 |
| 600 ms | 1 of 1 |

And in both failures **the pooled element's id at press time equalled what was submitted.** The pool re-pointed between the read and the click.

## That measurement refutes both shapes I put in the brief

I suggested carrying the painted id, or un-pooling the rows. Both are wrong, and the same figure kills them:

- **Carrying the painted id cannot detect anything.** The label and the id are written in the same synchronous paint, so the press-time id *is* the painted id — and both failures submitted exactly it.
- **Un-pooling changes only allocation.** The harm is not which object is reused; it is that the **screen position** holds a different order than the one whose label the player read.

The same figure also kills the "label and id in different publications" hypothesis.

## The fix is a third shape

A pure `assignPooledRows` (`src/ui/hud/pooled-row-binding.ts`, new):

- a place names one order **while that order is in the window**;
- a freed place **stays blank** for `BUILD_QUEUE_ROW_SETTLE_MS`;
- a blank place **keeps its box** while any place below it is occupied — no compaction under the pointer.

`CancelBuildOrder` is unchanged and no player-facing string changed.

**The settle window is 1000 ms and it is this change's weakest number**, said so by its author: the lower bound is measured at ~800 ms and everything above that is judgement.

## Two things that make this report worth more than the fix

**1. The pass measured its own first fix failing and corrected it.** That first attempt still got 2 of 3 presses wrong. The settle window and the no-compaction rule exist because of that second measurement, not because of the first design.

**2. It did not declare victory.** The third run, against the whole fix, still had **1 wrong press of 2** — but the instrument says the mechanism is no longer the pool: the element at those coordinates named *nothing* at press time, so the panel's own layout moved under the pointer between read and click. Candidates named and not separated: `paintDeliveries`' box above the queue, a `scrollIntoView`, the shortfall line. **That is a distinct defect on #862's surface**, and one press is not a distribution.

## A test that asserted the defect is overturned

`ui-build-queue.spec.ts`'s *"re-aims a pooled row"* case asserted the re-pointing as intended behaviour. Reversed, with both directions marked. #859's third side finding — a hidden row keeping a live-looking `data-order` — is fixed in the same pass.

## Red-then-green

Unit mutations 6/10 and 8/10 red, the property reporting **12** and **39** re-pointings against 0. The browser gate red under `rows[i] = orders[i]`, with the press submitting `order-02` where the row said `order-01`.

## Merge sequencing against #862

Both branches touch `src/ui/hud/build-panel.ts` and I asked each pass for its ranges. This one: `:12` (one import), `:576` (a new constant beside `BUILD_QUEUE_ROW_LIMIT`, which it did **not** change), `:1922`/`:1938`/`:1977` (the `QueueRow` interface, the cancel `onActivate` comment, the row factory, a new `emptyQueueRow`), `:2045`–`:2185` (`paintQueue`'s row loop and `unlisted`). It did not touch the row limit or the section's `collapsed: true` — both of which are #862's.

#862's own report says the two compose cleanly and that a 64-row pool makes this fix **more** valuable, not less. **Land this one first**, then #862 takes its `drawn` counter for `unlisted`.

## Same defect class, unswept — and one of them is sharper than this

Named by the pass and not fixed, index-bound pools in the same style:

- `paintDeliveries` in the same file
- **`staff-panel.ts`'s held-guard and roster pools** (`paintHeld` ~`:912`, dismiss rows ~`:965`) — **the dismiss one is sharper, because sacking somebody cannot be undone by waiting.**

That is the first follow-up I intend to file.

## One decision that may want an ADR, and one string that is the owner's

The queue list is **no longer in the crew's order**, which is unavoidable for a fixed pool and which `projectBuildQueue`'s own docblock argues the right way round. If an ordinal should come back into the row, that is a player-visible string and therefore the owner's.

## Gates

Both typechecks clean; `vite build` clean; `ui-build-queue.spec.ts` 11/11; targeted units 32/32. **The full `vitest run` of 388 files / 4,470 passed predates the settle-window commit** — the re-take was starved at load average 47.8 with three other agents' suites live, and five `tests/foundation` files went red there as `Test timed out in 5000ms` with no assertion. Reported unresolved rather than labelled a flake; #872 has since addressed that timeout at source.

items.title: Cancelling a pending object order is silent while the previous removal's "the money does not come back" sentence is still on the band — the same order cancelled two ways says two different things
items.body:
**Source:** `are-the-fixes-real`, round two/three consolidated report finding A1 (its own §11 first recommendation). Re-opened by the integrator's audit at `origin/main` v0.0.477 (`376b48bf`); every coordinate below was opened.

## What a player does

With the clock **paused**, so no tick can pass between the two presses:

1. Remove a standing bed with Build → `Remove`. The band says *"The object was removed — the money it cost does not come back."*
2. Remove a **pending** bed — an order still in flight — with the same control. **Nothing is said at all**, and the sentence from step 1 is still on screen, standing over the press that just happened.

That sentence is **false about the press it is standing over**: a cancelled order refunds.

## The code

Both presses enter `ObjectPlacementService.remove` (`src/simulation/objects/object-placement-service.ts:627`) and leave by different arms:

- **Standing object** — `:632` drops the registry row, `:651` calls `this.removalNotice?.recordObjectRemoved(tick)`. This is #945's fix and it works.
- **Pending order** — `:672-674`:

```ts
const pending = this.orderBuildingObjectAt(tile);
if (pending !== undefined) {
  this.orders.cancelOrder(pending.order.id);
  return { kind: 'order-cancelled', orderId: pending.order.id, objectId: pending.objectId, anchorTile: pending.order.location };
}
```

It calls `cancelOrder` **directly** and never enters the `CancelBuildOrder` branch that speaks.

The command handler adds nothing. The `RemoveObject` arm at `src/simulation/runtime/session-commands.ts:665` reaches `refusals.supersede(removeKey)` at `:696` on every non-refused outcome and records no event; `grep -n "events\.record" src/simulation/runtime/session-commands.ts` still returns the single `:539` (`recordDeliveryCancelled`).

**Byte-identical across every version these rounds played.** `git diff be244a24 376b48bf` over both files is empty — v0.0.469 through v0.0.477.

## The part the report gets wrong, and why it changes the fix

The consolidated report proposes *"pass the pending order's state to the event the other path already records."* **The code has already considered and refused that**, at `object-placement-service.ts:648-651`:

> The pending-order arm below records nothing: it refunds, and a sentence about money that does not come back is false of it.

That reasoning is correct and should not be reversed. **The defect is not that the silent arm says nothing — it is that the loud arm's sentence outlives its own press.** `refusals.supersede(removeKey)` at `:696` supersedes a *refusal*; nothing supersedes an *event*, so a true sentence about press 1 becomes a false sentence about press 2 by doing nothing at all.

## Acceptance

- After cancelling a pending object order, the band does not carry a sentence asserting that money was destroyed.
- The standing-object sentence still renders for the press that earned it (#945 stays closed).
- A test that pauses the clock, removes a standing object, then cancels a pending order, and asserts the band's content after the second press. Mutate the fix and watch it go red; report both outputs.

**No new player-visible string is required**, so `AGENTS.md` reservation 4 is not engaged: this is about the *lifetime* of a sentence already approved, not its wording.

items.title: Give the prison money, and money a way to become a wall (#89, #96)
items.body:
Closes the loop #96 decided and #89 has been waiting for. **A build order can reach `completed` in a real session for the first time.**

Built on the owner's decision to do the purchase loop before #91's starting stock, and on the assumption recorded [in this comment on #96](https://github.com/matmaxalez/lockstate/issues/96#issuecomment-5397099379) — read that first if you want the reasoning about what this does and does not decide.

## What was wrong

`createNewSimulationRuntime` registered one empty `Container` under `CONSTRUCTION_MATERIALS_CONTAINER_ID` and **nothing in the shipped codebase ever deposited into it**. `ConstructionSystem.update` called `materialsProvider.tryAllocate` on every scheduled tick, got `false`, and the order sat in `materials-pending` forever. Not a bug in construction — a missing half of the game.

## What this adds

- **`Treasury`** — a balance in **integer minor units**. Integer is not a formatting preference: a save carries this and the determinism fingerprint hashes it, and floating-point addition is not associative, so two runs applying the same purchases in a different order could disagree. `docs/DETERMINISM.md` states its rule for simulation state with no exception for money.
- **`ProcurementSystem`** — a purchase spends now and delivers after a delay. The pending queue is sorted by `(arrivesAtTick, orderId)`, never insertion order; `orderId` breaks the tie because the tick alone does not.
- **`src/content/procurement-catalog.ts`** — prices and one shared delivery delay, as a data module rather than a condition chain (`AGENTS.md` boundary 6).
- **A `PurchaseMaterials` command**, and `createSessionCommandHandler` to route it. It is the first command that is not a construction order, so the construction handler stays about construction rather than growing a money case.
- **The treasury and the pending queue in the save**, as an optional section — the same reason `SessionSnapshotBundle.simulation` is optional: a save written before the economy carries none, and a required field would make every one of them unrestorable.

The queue is carried rather than dropped because `purchase` spends *immediately*. A save taken between the payment and the arrival holds the only record that the money bought anything; dropping it would take the player's money and deliver nothing.

## What it deliberately does not decide

ADR 0017 is still `Proposed` and says plainly that nothing licenses shipping an economy until its three questions are answered. **Its status is untouched.** Its own closing note is the map — the loop *needs* answer 1 to have an income line, and *can begin* under answer 2 without answer 3 — and this stays inside that:

- **No income.** Nothing credits the treasury on a schedule. A starting balance is not an income basis, so what the state pays *for* (question 1) is completely open.
- **No insolvency policy.** The balance cannot go negative — `spend` refuses rather than overdrawing, which is validation and not policy — and with nothing paying in, a negative balance is unreachable. Question 3 is open and not needed.
- **Answer 2 only in its weak direction.** Prices do not vary and delivery time is uniform, so there is nothing to gain by buying early. That is what makes "just-in-time by default, holding permitted but never required" true rather than merely stated.

Every number is a placeholder and says so at its declaration.

## What it is half of, stated rather than implied

#96 describes the loop as money → purchase → **delivery arrives at the bay → carry jobs move it to the site** → provider consumes it. The middle is **not** here: no session instantiates `room.delivery-bay`, which is declared content with no consumer (#141), so there is no bay to deliver to. Building one means deciding where a new prison's bay sits and when a carry job is raised — scenario design and logistics policy.

So a delivery lands directly in the container construction draws from. That is scaffolding, and it is in `ProcurementSystem`'s own header and in `new-session.ts` rather than left to be inferred from the absence of a bay.

## The determinism pin caught it, and the ADR 0009 step came to nothing

`tests/determinism/kernel-system-order.test.ts` failed on the new system — exactly as designed. Its comment requires that updating the list be accompanied, per ADR 0009, by retiring incompatible challenge submissions through the definition allow-lists.

**There is nothing in this repository to retire**, and that is recorded at the pin so the next person does not hunt for a list that does not exist: `allowedGameVersions`/`allowedContentVersions` are fields on a *challenge definition*, definitions live in the trusted tier's `challenge_definitions` table, and the migrations create and grant on that table while seeding no rows. The obligation is real and simply not yet reachable — a different thing from being satisfied.

## Mutations: nine applied, four survived, all four fixed

| # | mutation | first pass | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | delivery never deposits — restores #89 exactly | KILLED (2) | — |
| 2 | purchase does not spend | KILLED (2) | — |
| 3 | deliver instantly | KILLED (1) | — |
| 4 | arrived deliveries stay queued | KILLED (1) | — |
| 5 | `economy` dropped from `captureSessionSystems` | **SURVIVED** | KILLED |
| 6 | `restoreSessionSystems` ignores `economy` | **SURVIVED** | KILLED |
| 7 | the purchase command routed nowhere | KILLED (1) | — |
| 8 | pending queue unsorted | **SURVIVED** | KILLED |
| 9 | refund credits `0` instead of what was paid | **SURVIVED** | KILLED |

The four survivors were all gaps in **my** tests, not in the code:

- **5 and 6** — my round-trip test called `procurement.restore(procurement.snapshot())`, which proves the codec and says nothing about whether the *save* carries it. Rewritten to go through `captureSessionSnapshot` → JSON → `restoreSimulationRuntime`, the real boundary.
- **8** — nothing asserted the ordering. Same-tick deliveries of the same item are indistinguishable once deposited, so the new test buys two *different* items in both orders and reads the queue.
- **9** — `cancel` had no test at all. It has no caller in `src/` yet, and an untested public method on a system that spends money is worse than one that does not exist, so it is tested rather than deleted: the refund is the recorded `paidMinorUnits`, never a recomputation from the catalog, which would refund today's price for yesterday's purchase the moment prices move.

## Doc-truth

Four sentences this falsified, corrected rather than left standing:

- `src/ui/hud/view-model.ts:77` — *"there is no economy system yet"*. There is one; what there still is not is anything that credits the treasury, and the rule that keeps the strip truthful is unchanged.
- `src/content/default-locale-en.ts:97` — same claim, in the locale header.
- `docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md:344` — *"`wageBand` exists in content, and there is no economy"*. Rewritten: there is no **payroll**; nothing pays anyone.
- `src/simulation/construction/definition.ts:48` — written *ahead* of this change, predicting that the vocabulary check would matter "the moment anything deposits stock using item catalog ids — which is exactly what a purchase and delivery will do". It did, and the arrival was uneventful because that check existed. Its tense is corrected.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm test` 162 files, 1,667 passed / 1 skipped; `pnpm build` produced verified Cloudflare production output.

The end-to-end test drives the **real** kernel, decoder and systems and deposits nothing by hand — a test that seeded the materials would prove the construction half and say nothing about whether a player can get them. It asserts the world actually changed at the end, because an order reaching `completed` is not the same claim as a wall existing.

## What comes next, and is not here

- **A player cannot spend the money.** There is no HUD control and no balance on screen; the purchase reaches the simulation before it reaches the interface. Catalog keys arrive with the control that needs them.
- **A refused purchase tells nobody.** `createSessionCommandHandler` drops the outcome, and the comment says so: the kernel's handler returns `void` and the worker's reply acknowledges receipt, not effect. It is the same problem #225 solved for a refused wall and needs the same route.
