items.title: Stop seeding every prison at zero (#479)
items.body:
Closes #479. Every prison anyone has ever played was seeded at **0**.

## Confirmed, re-derived rather than taken on trust

- `src/main.ts` holds the only `new SessionController` under `src/`, and it passed no `masterSeed`. `git log -S"masterSeed" --oneline -- src/main.ts` is empty for the entire history.
- `session-controller.ts:68` was `this.masterSeed = options.masterSeed ?? 0`, and every `createPrison` used that one field.
- `src/main.ts:795`'s comment — *"the variation comes from `prisoners.classification`, seeded, and not from a figure picked here"* — is about `ADMISSION_REQUEST`'s constants. It is load-bearing evidence in the other direction: the only variation path is an RNG stream that was never actually varied.

**The persistence half is genuinely already fixed** and is untouched here. `captureSessionSnapshot` always writes `masterSeed`, `restoreSimulationRuntime` prefers the bundle's seed over any argument, and both production restore call sites pass none — so the bundle always wins. `tests/integration/session-save-master-seed.test.ts` already proves the round trip and that a V1 save without the field restores at 0. Re-run, still green, unchanged.

## A wrinkle the issue did not spell out

`masterSeed` lived on `SessionController` as one field for the controller's whole lifetime, and `save-panel.ts`'s `requestCreate` lets a player press **New Prison** repeatedly without a page reload. So the obvious fix — draw one random seed at boot — would still have given every prison created in one page session the *same* seed. The draw is therefore per `createPrison` call, via a new `generateMasterSeed?: () => number` option defaulting to `() => 0` so every existing caller and test is unaffected.

## The three decisions

1. **Where the seed comes from:** `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint32Array(1))`, drawn in `src/main.ts` — outside `src/simulation/`'s import graph, verified against how `tests/determinism/ambient-nondeterminism-contract.test.ts` walks outward — and handed in as a plain number. **Not `Date.now()`**: `docs/DETERMINISM.md` permits exactly one time reader (`FixedStepClock`, pacing only), and a clock read here would be a second one with a different job, which the document carves out no room for. Real entropy needs no such exception, and matches this file's existing convention — `crypto.randomUUID()` is already used for `transactionId`/`orderId`.
2. **Survival across a save:** nothing new needed, per the finding above. Only the value a *new* runtime is built with changes; capture and restore are untouched.
3. **Prisons already saved at seed 0:** untouched, and correctly so. Absence still means 0 (ADR 0038 §4), `SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 5, no migration. They keep restoring at 0 and keep producing the world they always produced.

## Documentation rot corrected in both directions

ADR 0038 §4, `docs/PERSISTENCE.md` and a `restore-session.ts` doc comment each asserted, in the present tense, that *production has never supplied another value*. That was true and is now false. The rule they state — absence means 0, no schema bump — is explicitly unchanged and not reopened.

## Evidence

New guard `tests/integration/session-master-seed-variety.test.ts`. Per #375 it does **not** pass two literals: it obtains each seed by giving the controller a `generateMasterSeed` built the same way `main.ts` builds it, and covers both shapes — one controller with two `createPrison` calls, and two controllers.

Mutation RED, `createPrison` hand-reverted to `this.masterSeed ?? 0`:
```
expected +0 not to be +0 // Object.is equality   (both new cases)
Test Files  1 failed (1) | Tests  2 failed (2)
```
Restored by hand → GREEN, `1 passed (1) | 2 passed (2)`.

**The no-jsdom trap, addressed rather than stepped in:** `src/main.ts` boots Phaser and touches `document` at module scope, so it cannot be imported under `environment: 'node'` at all. The new `generateMasterSeed` is pure, so the test exercises the identical mechanism rather than importing `main.ts`, and the test file says so in a comment.

Gates: `tsc -b` clean; full suite **306 files / 3500 passed / 1 skipped** (pre-existing); production build succeeds. The `pnpm build`/`verify` wrappers shell out to `pnpm` and hit `ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR` inside a worktree, so their constituent binaries were run directly.

## No ADR, and no player-visible surface

This is wiring inside architecture ADR 0038, ADR 0009 and `docs/DETERMINISM.md` already settled; none of ADR 0038's four open questions touches seed sourcing. No number was taken.

**Nothing shows or accepts a seed.** A "new prison from seed" control is a player-visible feature reserved by `AGENTS.md`'s fourth exclusion — recommended, not built.

## Left undone

The historical line-number citations to `session-controller.ts` in `docs/research/audit-2026-08-26/**` and `docs/adr/STATUS-QUEUE.md` are dated snapshots already understood to drift, and were deliberately not rewritten.

items.title: [Economy] Undoing a paid-for build order strands the money: `ProcurementSystem.cancel` is the only credit path and has no producer
items.body:
**Not reachable on `main` today. It becomes reachable the moment #282 lands**, because #282 is what first gives a player a way to spend. Filing it now so the gap is recorded before it goes live rather than after.

**This is not #114.** #114 refuted an alleged *materials* double-spend and confirmed the brick axis is fixed and guarded by `tests/unit/operations-construction-integration.test.ts:142`. This is the **money** axis, which #114 does not touch: bricks come back, the minor units do not.

## The claim

`PurchaseMaterials` debits the treasury at purchase time. Nothing that a player can reach ever credits it back. So a player who buys materials for a build order and then undoes that order keeps the bricks as unattached stock and has permanently lost the money, with no affordance that explains it and none that recovers it.

## Measured, by execution

Driven through `createNewSimulationRuntime` + `Kernel.step()` with the real `packCommand`/`unpackCommand` — not by calling `procurement.purchase()` directly. Raw output:

```
=== money across purchase, build and undo ===
session start                         : balance=25000 bricks=0
after PurchaseMaterials (spends now)  : balance=24920 bricks=0 pendingDeliveries=1
after delivery + allocation           : #0=completed balance=24920 bricks=0 pendingDeliveries=0 topEdge@0,0=1
after Undo of the completed order     : #0=cancelled balance=24920 bricks=2 topEdge@0,0=0

=== money, delivery in flight, and undo ===
purchased (spent, delivery in flight) : tick=  1 balance=24920 bricks=0 pendingDeliveries=1 order=none
order placed, waiting on materials    : tick= 11 balance=24920 bricks=0 pendingDeliveries=1 order=materials-pending
UNDO while the delivery is in flight  : tick= 12 balance=24920 bricks=0 pendingDeliveries=1 order=cancelled
300 ticks later                       : tick=300 balance=24920 bricks=2 pendingDeliveries=0 order=cancelled
procurement.cancel("buy-1") DIRECTLY  : returned true
after the direct refund               : tick=  1 balance=25000 bricks=0 pendingDeliveries=0 order=none
```

Three things this pins:

1. **Undo returns materials, never money.** `cancelOrder` releases `materialsAllocated` back to the container (`src/simulation/construction/system.ts:245-248`) — that is the `0 → 2` bricks. The balance does not move on any path.
2. **The money never attaches to the build order at all.** `PurchaseMaterials` spends at purchase time (`src/simulation/economy/procurement.ts:126`) against a *purchase* `orderId`, which is minted fresh per press and is not the build order's id. So there is nothing for `cancelOrder` to refund even in principle.
3. **A refund path exists, works, and is unreachable.** `ProcurementSystem.cancel` (`procurement.ts:142-148`) restores the balance exactly — `25000` in the last two lines. `grep -rn "\.cancel(" src/` finds only `navigation-system.ts:78` and `job-system.ts:219`; neither is this. It is callable only from a test.

Undoing while a delivery is still in flight is the sharpest case: the money is gone, the order is cancelled, and the bricks arrive 288 ticks later as stock attached to nothing.

## The doc that already says this, describing a credit no session can produce

`docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md:359-361` states that the only thing which credits the treasury is a cancelled purchase's refund via `ProcurementSystem.cancel`. That sentence is literally true of the code and describes an event no player can cause. It is worth re-reading once this is resolved, because whichever way it is resolved changes it.

## Why this is a `PurchaseMaterials` gap and not a `CancelBuildOrder` gap

The tempting fix — wire `CancelBuildOrder` and refund from there — does not work, and the reason is the id. A refund has to name the **purchase** `orderId`, and a build order does not know it; the two ids are independent by construction. Recovering the money needs a producer for a *purchase*-cancel keyed on the purchase id, which no command in `simulationCommandSchema` currently expresses.

That also means this is not blocked on the separate question of whether `CancelBuildOrder` should be wired at all (measured separately: undo's unit is a transaction and cancel's is an order, so they are not substitutes, but a cancel is invisible to `undoStack`/`redoStack` — an undo-model decision).

## What needs deciding, not implementing

Three candidate resolutions, and picking between them is a product/economy decision rather than an implementation detail, so per `CLAUDE.md` it wants a written decision rather than a branch:

1. **Refund on undo.** Tie the purchase to the build order it was bought for, so cancelling the order cancels any purchase still in flight. Changes what a purchase *is* — currently it buys stock, not stock-for-an-order — and that is a persisted-shape change.
2. **A purchase-cancel command with its own surface.** Honest and additive, but needs a list of in-flight purchases to cancel from, which is new HUD surface and a new projection.
3. **Decide the money is simply spent, and say so on screen.** Cheapest and possibly correct for a management game: materials bought are materials owned, and the stock stays usable by the next order. Then the work is a locale string and a doc correction, not a mechanism — and `ProcurementSystem.cancel` should arguably be deleted rather than left as an unreachable credit path.

I lean toward **3** on the grounds that the bricks genuinely remain usable, so nothing is actually lost except the player's understanding — which is a reporting problem, and #283 has just built the channel for reporting. But it is a call about how the economy should feel, and I am not making it in code.

## Related

- #282 — makes this reachable; it is the change that first lets a player spend.
- #283 — builds the refusal channel that resolution 3 would report through.
- #89 — the missing purchase producer that #282 closes.
- #114 — the *materials* axis, refuted and guarded; explicitly not this.
- #96 — the treasury readout that displays the balance this strands.

items.title: Give the player a way to spend the treasury (#89)
items.body:
Closes #89.

`PurchaseMaterials` has had a schema, a decoder, a session command router, a system and a save representation since #249, and **nothing in `src/` could construct one**. So the only thing that could buy a brick was a test, and every build order placed in a real session reached `materials-pending` and stayed there: the ghost appeared and the wall never did.

The surface is a quantity stepper on the Build panel. Where it sits is a measurement, not a preference.

## Why it is a disclosure, in numbers

Measured on the assembled page (Build tab, one prison saved, coordinates folded — the state a player arrives in), **before any change**:

| viewport | body box | body content | panel overflow | catalogue | map block | last section | header → fold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1280×720 | 351 | 351 | 0 | 140 | 149.8 | 45 | 8.3 |
| 1440×900 | 351 | 351 | 0 | 140 | 149.8 | 45 | 8.3 |
| 1024×768 | 351 | 351 | 0 | 140 | 149.8 | 45 | 8.3 |
| 900×600 | **291** | **291** | 0 | **135.9** | 94.2 | 45 | 7.9 |
| 375×812 | 338 | 338 | 0 | 140 | 136.6 | 45 | 8.4 |

At 900×600 the rail is 482.8px and `.hud__aside` is pinned exactly on its 25 % floor (120.7px = 25 % of 482.8), so the rail is over-subscribed and the Build panel gets the remainder. The catalogue sits at 135.9px against its 132px two-row floor: **3.9px is the entire budget** a new always-visible block has there.

Every candidate was measured against that 3.9px. A collapsed section of its own is 45px (1px border plus a 44px header). A bare row of controls is 44px. Deleting the arm hint at ≤700px buys 13.2px plus a 4px gutter. A one-row catalogue floor buys 44px and makes the shipped two-entry list scroll. `.hud__aside { min-height: 0 }` was already ruled out by #174 — a 41.1px box over 240px of save-panel content. **Nothing always-visible fits**, and #174 closed exactly this overflow one commit earlier.

So: a disclosure that costs nothing until it is opened. The "Buy" toggle shares the arm button's row, which is `--tap-target` tall whether one button or two sit in it; the stepper, the priced buy button and a delivery hint live in a `hidden` row inside `.hud-build__map`.

**After, arrival state: byte-identical at all five viewports** — every cell in the table above is unchanged, and the four regression assertions #174 added pass unweakened at all five.

Open state (player-initiated):

| viewport | body box | body content | panel overflow | map block | buy row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1280×720 | 373 | 492 | 119 | 307.3 | 149.6 |
| 1440×900 | 508 | 508 | **0** | 307.3 | 149.6 |
| 1024×768 | 409 | 492 | 83 | 307.3 | 149.6 |
| 900×600 | 291 | 412 | 121 | 226.6 | 128.4 |
| 375×812 | 404 | 479 | 75 | 294.1 | 149.6 |

That is the same honest scroll `hud.css` already documents for the expanded numeric fallback (187px at 1280×720): the player opened it, the panel absorbs its own excess, and the wheel scrolls it. Opening also scrolls the row into view, because a disclosure that reveals a control below the fold has not revealed it.

## Wiring

- A new `purchase-materials` `HudIntent` carrying an item id and a quantity — ids and numbers only. The HUD does not know a `PurchaseMaterials` command exists.
- A branch in `src/main.ts` builds the command and mints `order-${crypto.randomUUID()}`, matching `identifierSchema` and `PlaceBuildOrder`'s existing shape. A fresh id per purchase, because `ProcurementSystem.purchase` refuses a duplicate.
- Prices, per-placement quantity, the item's `nameKey` and `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` reach the panel through `HudBuildableViewModel.material`, projected at the composition root from `BUILDABLE_REGISTRY`, `src/content/procurement-catalog.ts` and the item catalog. The panel holds no price table.
- A refused purchase reaches the player on the refusal line #207 built. The worker drops the outcome of `procurement.purchase` — the kernel's command handler returns `void` — so the composition root refuses before sending, against the balance the worker last published, and the throw paints the line and marks the button.
- `tests/foundation/unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts` moves from five unproduced commands to four and from one produced to two, and its `PurchaseMaterials` entry is deleted. The gate fails in both directions, so neither the count nor the list could be edited alone.

## Mutation results

Every entry run against the merged tree, each reverted afterwards, each `git diff --stat` confirming the file really changed.

| # | mutation | verified by | before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | `type: 'PurchaseMaterials'` → `'MUTANT-…'` in `main.ts` | `unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts` | 6 passed → **3 failed / 3 passed** |
| M2 | disable the affordability guard | app-shell "buys materials" | 1 passed → **1 failed** (`.hud__refusal` hidden) |
| M3 | `.hud-build__buy:not([hidden])` → `.hud-build__buy` | app-shell #88 sweep | 1 passed → **1 failed** ("scrolls on arrival at 1280x720") |
| M4 | quantity ceiling → the typed value | ui-shell "clamped" | 1 passed → **1 failed** (`999999` vs `100000`) |
| M5 | drop the quantity reset on selection change | ui-shell "follows the selection" | 1 passed → **1 failed** (`Buy 2 …` vs `Buy 3 …`) |
| M6 | `dispatchCommand` → ungated `runReported` | ui-shell "one gated intent" | 1 passed → **1 failed** (`failedControls` empty) |
| M7 | drop `scrollIntoView` on open | app-shell "buys materials" | 1 passed → **1 passed — SURVIVED** |
| M7′ | same, after moving the assertion into the #88 sweep | app-shell #88 sweep | 1 passed → **1 failed** at 1280×720 |
| M8 | invert the `procurableMaterial` guard in `main.ts` | app-shell "buys materials" | 1 passed → **1 failed** (toggle never appears) |

**M7 is the instructive one.** The first placement of the "the revealed control is inside the panel's visible box" assertion was in the producer test, at 1280×800 — a viewport where the panel does not overflow when the row opens, so the assertion held with the `scrollIntoView` deleted and proved nothing. The mutation caught that. Moving it into the five-viewport #88 sweep, where the panel really does overflow at four of the five, made it bite: M7′ fails at 1280×720 with *"opening the row revealed a control the player cannot see"*.

`.hud-build__buy:not([hidden])` (M3) is worth calling out too: an author `display: flex` beats the user agent's `display: none`, and without the guard the panel arrives 121px over its box at 900×600 — #174 re-opened by a declaration order. That was measured before the guard existed, not reasoned about.

## Guards added

- `app-shell.spec.ts` drives the real page and tees `postMessage`: pressing Buy sends one `PurchaseMaterials` with the item and quantity the stepper showed and an identifier-shaped fresh `orderId`; a second press gets another id; an unaffordable total is refused with nothing sent and the thrown English never on screen (ADR 0011).
- The #88 reachability sweep now visits the buy-open state at all five viewports, with the rail invariants and the in-view check above.
- `ui-shell.spec.ts` covers the closed disclosure, the priced label, the stepper, the clamp to `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY`, the quantity resetting when the material changes, one gated intent per press, the refusal on the button, and a buildable nothing sells offering no purchase at all.
- `tests/integration/economy-build-loop.test.ts` keeps the order → purchase → delivery → `completed` → `world.getTopEdge` loop and now derives its quantities and price from the same two content modules `main.ts` reads, so a buildable nobody sells fails there rather than shipping as a buy control that could only be refused.

## Doc-truth

Sentences in `view-model.ts`, `projection.ts`, `messages.ts`, `default-locale-en.ts`, `session-commands.ts`, `tests/unit/ui-hud-messages.test.ts` and `docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` (gaps 32 and 32a) that said the HUD shows a balance and nothing that spends it are rewritten rather than deleted. Gap 32a is marked closed for the player while the empty starting container stays true. `default-locale-en.ts`'s HUD header claimed *"No money, funds or cost keys exist"* while defining `hud.status.funds` — already false before this change, and corrected here. The `min-height` sum in `hud.css` is unchanged and now says why: the buy row is the map block's fourth child, `hidden` on arrival, so it lays out no box and creates no gap.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -b --pretty false` — exit 0, no output.
- `npx vitest run` — **170 files passed, 1814 passed | 1 skipped (1815)**.
- `npx vite build` — clean, exit 0; only the pre-existing >500 kB chunk warning.
- Browser suite — **108 passed, 1 failed**: `every runtime atlas … decodes at its authored size`, the documented Git-LFS baseline failure in this container.

## What this does not do, and why

1. **The buy control does not appear "only when the materials are short."** Knowing that needs the construction container's stock, and no projection or protocol channel carries it — `SimulationStatusCounts` is a flat record of integers whose equality check documents that property. Widening it is a real protocol change with ripples through `docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` §8. The disclosure costs the same zero height; gap 32 now records the stock projection as the thing that would let the control become a prompt.
2. **A refusal the worker makes still has no route back.** `createSessionCommandHandler` drops `procurement.purchase`'s outcome; the kernel's handler returns `void` and a command reply acknowledges receipt, not effect. The composition root's check covers the case a player can actually reach — asking for more than the prison has ever had. Two cases still get past it and are named in `main.ts`: a balance that moved in the last 500 ms, and several purchases queued against a figure none has been deducted from yet, most visibly with the clock paused. Left recorded on #96.
3. **There is no unit-level test of the producer.** `src/main.ts` imports Phaser, constructs a `Worker` and runs at import, so no Vitest file can execute it. The producer is proved by the foundation gate (that it is written) and by the browser tee (that pressing Buy sends it).
4. **A buildable made of two materials would get a buy control for one of them.** `purchasableMaterialFor` takes the first requirement anything sells. Both shipped buildables require exactly one, so "first" and "only" agree today; a multi-material buy surface is undesigned rather than implemented and broken, and it is stated in `main.ts` and in gap 32 rather than hidden.

items.title: [Audit] What a player can actually do: one of thirteen systems does observable work, and the shortest path to a loop
items.body:
An end-to-end reachability audit traced from the real composition root (`src/main.ts`) outward, not from the tests. **This question is not answered anywhere else in the repository**, and the answer is short.

Claims are **VERIFIED** (read and/or executed) or **INFERRED**. Executed claims were driven through `createNewSimulationRuntime` and `Kernel.step()` — the same runtime the worker builds — from throwaway scripts outside the repository. Raw output is quoted.

---

## 1. What a player can do today

1. **Load the page and look at an empty grey world.** The worker is `uninitialized`; the strip reads `Day --` and zeros.
2. **Press "New prison".** The only thing on the page that starts a simulation. You get a 32×32 square of dirt with one owned chunk, and a save.
3. **Look at the prison.** Pan with the middle button, WASD or arrows; zoom with wheel, `+`, `−`; one-finger drag and two-finger pinch on touch. **Nothing the camera does reaches the simulation.**
4. **Start and stop time.** Pause / Play / Fast-forward genuinely work. One in-game day is two minutes of real time at ×1.
5. **Switch to Build and choose "Brick wall" or "Wooden door".** The only two entries.
6. **Press "Place on map", then click or drag along a tile edge.** A translucent brown box appears. It is a build *order*.
7. **Watch that box stay translucent forever.** It never becomes a wall — there is no way in the entire interface to buy the bricks it waits for. It survives every save and reload.
8. **Type coordinates instead.** Same outcome. **A coordinate outside the owned chunk is silently discarded** — nothing appears and nothing says why.
9. **Save, load, delete, export.** All work. Export downloads a file the application cannot import back.
10. **`?actors=demo`** shows three scripted sprites walking in a circle. A rendering demonstration, not simulation state.

**That is the complete list.** The single mechanical consequence a player can produce is item 6: a ghost outline.

---

## 2. The proof, executed

`createNewSimulationRuntime(0)`, one `PlaceBuildOrder` exactly as `main.ts` builds it at tile (16,16), then 2,000 ticks — 100 in-game seconds:

```
[A] after 2000 ticks state=materials-pending progress=0 failReason=undefined
[A] treasury=25000
[A] chunk topEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

`[[0,1024]]` is 1,024 run-length-encoded zeroes: **no wall anywhere in the world.**

The same runtime with one `PurchaseMaterials` command inserted first:

```
[B] state=completed treasury=24600
[B] chunk topEdge=[[0,528],[1,1],[0,495]]
```

Index 528 = `16 × 32 + 16` — the exact tile. **The construction pipeline is complete and correct; the only missing link in the whole chain is a producer for one command.**

---

## 3. Thirteen systems run every tick. One does work a player can see.

Read from a live runtime's `systemExecutionOrder`:

| System | Iterates | Non-empty in a reachable session? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prisoners.intake` | live prisoner entities | **No** — `admitPrisoner` has no caller in `src/` |
| `prisoners.needs-decay` | same | **No** (see #259) |
| **`construction`** | `orderedOrders()` | **Yes — the one reachable system.** Stalls at `materials-pending` |
| `procurement` | `this.pending` | **No** — returns on line 156 every tick, 20 times a second, forever |
| `navigation` | graph + queue | **Partially.** `ensureGraph()` does real work; **nothing reads its output** — no route is ever requested |
| `prisoners.actions` | prisoner query | No |
| `operations.jobs` | `activeJobs()` | **No** — `submitCarryItem` has no caller |
| `contraband.intelligence` | decays an empty ledger | No |
| `security.deployment` | `allGuardIds()` | **No** — `GuardRoster.hire` has no caller |
| `security.patrol` | same | No |
| `incidents.trigger` | `sectorIds` (empty) | No |
| `contraband.search` | queued orders (none) | No |
| `incidents.response` | `openIncidents()` | No |

**Eleven of thirteen iterate permanently empty collections.** One more does real computation nothing reads.

### Three subsystems are not even registered

- **`TopologyManager`** (229 lines) is constructed, exposed on `SimulationRuntime.topology`, and **`update()` is never called anywhere in `src/`**. It has no `id`/`order`/`schedule`, **so it cannot be registered with the kernel at all.** Room enclosure detection never runs.
- **`UtilityNetwork`** — two instances built, no `update`, and `addNode`/`connect`/`evaluate` have no caller outside their own module.
- **`ContainerRegistry`, `JobBoard`, `JobWorkerPool`** — built empty; only the construction container is registered and nothing is ever put in it.

---

## 4. Three findings worth their own attention

### A finished wooden door writes nothing and creates no door

`edgeNumericIdFor` returns `0` for `category: 'object'`, so `finalizeConstruction` only bumps the geometry revision. Executed:

```
[C] door state=completed
[C] topEdge=[[0,1024]]  leftEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

It exists only as a 0.55-tile-high brown slab drawn from the order list. `DoorRegistry.register` is called from exactly one place — restoring from a snapshot. **Nothing creates the first door.**

### A refused order gives the player no feedback of any kind

The command reply acknowledges *receipt*, not effect: `state-machine.ts:524-535` posts `status: 'queued'` as soon as the kernel accepts it. A `failReason` of `out-of-bounds` or `unowned-land` is mapped to `undefined` by `phaseOf` and drawn as nothing. Executed, typing `100, 100` into fields that have no `min`/`max`:

```
[E] far order state=failed failReason=out-of-bounds
```

The refusal line stays hidden because the command *was* queued successfully, and no ghost appears. (`x = 2e9`, `x = -5`, `x = 9e12` all fail cleanly — **no player-reachable crash was found down any path.**)

### `ConstructionSystem` has a complete undo/redo model that nothing can reach

`undo()`/`redo()` are transaction-grouped and snapshot-safe; `main.ts:492` mints one `transactionId` per gesture *specifically* so a twelve-segment wall undoes as one. There is no control, no binding and no intent that can trigger it — `grep` for `KeyZ`, `ctrlKey`, `metaKey` in `src/` returns **zero matches**.

Five of six commands have no producer: `PurchaseMaterials`, `CancelBuildOrder`, `Undo`, `Redo`, `ZoneRoom` — and `ZoneRoom`'s consumer is itself a no-op (`case 'ZoneRoom': break;`).

---

## 5. Where each on-screen number comes from

Fresh session, before any tick:

```
[D] {"prisoners":0,"prisonersInIntake":0,"prisonersHighRisk":0,"staff":0,
     "staffUnassigned":0,"rooms":0,"roomCapacity":0,"roomOccupants":0,
     "activeIncidents":0,"contrabandDiscovered":0,"treasuryMinorUnits":25000}
```

| On screen | Real or constant? |
| --- | --- |
| **Prisoners** | Real projection, **permanently 0** |
| Cell occupancy bar | **Never rendered** — `prisonerCapacity` is hard-coded `0` on the main thread, so the bar is removed |
| **Staff** / **Rooms** / **Incidents** / **Contraband** | Real projections, all permanently 0 |
| **Funds** | Real value, **effectively a constant 25,000** — nothing credits it and the only spender is unreachable |
| **Day N** and **% through the day** | **Real and moving.** The only figures that change |
| **Alerts** | **Always "No active alerts."** `viewModel.alerts` is assigned nowhere except a literal `[]` |
| **Minimap** | **Constant string** "Minimap is not available yet" |
| **World canvas** | Real. **Actors are always empty** — the feed's own comment says the bundle *does* carry prisoner tile positions and this feed does not decode them |

**Two projections produce nothing anyone reads:** `projectWorldForRendering` has no consumer at all — the renderer decodes the *save bundle's* world section instead, so the purpose-built render projection is dead and the save format is doing its job. And `projectStatusStrip`'s `clock` and `regime` blocks are computed and discarded.

---

## 6. The built/reachable line, measured

**207 of 256 `.ts` files under `src/` are reachable from the composition root; 49 are not.** Excluding barrels, the 29 substantive never-imported modules total **3,978 lines**: all of `services/telemetry/`, `services/entitlements/`, `services/challenges/`, `persistence/cloud/`, and three presentation projections.

**Reachable-but-never-called exports**, each verified by grep: `TopologyManager.update`, `admitPrisoner`, `GuardRoster.hire`, `JobBoard.submitCarryItem`, `UtilityNetwork.addNode/connect/evaluate`, `resolveEscapeOpportunity`, `buildRiotRegimeSchedule`, `toIncidentAlert`, `summarizeIncidents`, nine of the ten presentation projections, `remapKeyboardBinding`, `saveInputSettings`, `loadAccessibilitySettings`, `SessionController.importInto`.

**Content:** 62 declared ids, **53 with no reference in `src/` outside `src/content/`**. The nine that have one are all referenced by a system that never runs on live data. Zero contraband categories, zero security grades, zero staff roles and zero object ids are referenced from `src/` at all.

**One unused message key:** `HUD_MESSAGE_KEY.buildNote` is declared and never rendered — the only one of 56 with no render site. Its English is *"An order is queued now and built while the clock runs."* Given §2, it is fortunate it is not on screen.

---

## 7. The shortest path to a playable loop, ordered

Wiring only. No new architecture, no ADR, no new abstraction.

**Step 1 — Make a placed wall become a wall.** The highest-value change in the repository; everything downstream is proven to work. **The owner has chosen the surface: a quantity stepper on the Build panel** (not the auto-purchase this audit first sketched). That work is in flight. What the player gets: the ghost turns solid, and the **Funds** chip drops. Two of six status numbers start moving. It also makes insolvency visible — 25,000 buys 156 walls, and `spend` refuses rather than overdrawing — which leads straight to step 2.

**Step 2 — Tell the player when the simulation refuses.** Without it, "out of money" is indistinguishable from today's bug. Two facts currently vanish: `PurchaseOutcome` is discarded at `session-commands.ts:42` (the code says so), and `failReason` never leaves the simulation. The machinery already exists and has **never had a producer**: `HudViewModel.alerts` is fully implemented, with severity badges and an empty-state row. Publish a small refusal field on the existing `simulation/status-counts` channel — no new message kind — and map it in `main.ts`'s existing listener.

**Step 3 — Make `ZoneRoom` register a room instance.** Its handler is `break;`. `RoomInstanceRegistry.register` takes exactly what the command carries plus a capacity and capability list. **Do this before step 4:** `IntakeSystem` marks an arrival `'failed'` when no instance of the required room type exists *at all*, so admitting into a prison with no cell is a structural dead end, not a wait.

**Step 4 — Admit one prisoner.** Executed proof that the rest is ready — one `room.cell` registered, `admitPrisoner` called, 600 ticks:

```
entity=0 intakeStage=4 (completed)
metrics={"completedCount":1,"failedCount":0,"accommodationBacklogTicks":0}
counts={"prisoners":1,...,"rooms":1,"roomCapacity":1,"roomOccupants":1,...}
position=10,10  (the cell's anchor tile)
```

**Two calls turn three of the six status numbers real.** Fix #259 in the same change, or the prisoner is inert.

**Step 5 — Decode actors into the render frame.** `actors: []` is one line, and the feed's comment says the data is already in the bundle. `ActorLayer` is built, the atlases load, and `DemoActorFeed` proves the sprite path end to end. **This is the moment the prison stops being a diagram.**

**Step 6 — Reach the undo that already exists.** A binding plus a case, and a fully built feature returns.

---

## What is deliberately not claimed

- The page was not run in a browser. Every DOM/Phaser statement is from source and marked INFERRED; every simulation statement marked VERIFIED was executed.
- A passing test was never treated as evidence a player can reach something. Where a test is the only consumer, that is what is said.
- **No player-visible consequence is attributed to any unreachable subsystem.** `TopologyManager` never running, telemetry being unwired and 53 unconsumed ids cost a player nothing *today* — precisely because there is no loop for them to be part of. The finding is the gap between built and reachable, not an invented symptom.

items.title: Assert money conservation across build orders and undo (#285)
items.body:
Addresses #285 by measuring it. **It does not wire a refund, and the measurement is the reason.**

## The reproduction, and what it showed

#285's title is *"undoing a paid-for build order strands the money"*. I wrote the test that claim describes — place a build order, assert the treasury was debited, undo, assert the balance — and drove it through `createNewSimulationRuntime`, the real `packCommand` decoder and the real session command router. Raw failing output:

```
start                       : balance=25000 bricks=0
after PlaceBuildOrder       : balance=25000 bricks=0 state=materials-pending

 FAIL  #285 reproduction: undoing a paid-for build order
AssertionError: placing the build order must debit the treasury:
  expected 25000 to be 24920

- Expected
+ Received

- 24920
+ 25000
```

**A build order is not paid for.** `PlaceBuildOrder` reaches `ConstructionSystem.submitOrder` and touches no `Treasury` on any path. What a player pays for is a *purchase*: `PurchaseMaterials` buys stock, minted from its own Build-panel control since #282, with an `orderId` no build order knows. That is #285's own "why this is a `PurchaseMaterials` gap and not a `CancelBuildOrder` gap" section reached from the other end — there is no payment attached to a build order for an undo to strand.

## Nor is the money lost

The second measurement, valuing stock and in-flight deliveries at what was paid for them:

```
session start                    : balance=25000 stock=0 allocated=0 inFlight=0  total=25000
after PurchaseMaterials          : balance=24920 stock=0 allocated=0 inFlight=80 total=25000
after PlaceBuildOrder            : balance=24920 stock=0 allocated=0 inFlight=80 total=25000
after delivery + build completes : balance=24920 stock=0 allocated=2 inFlight=0  total=25000
after Undo                       : balance=24920 stock=2 allocated=0 inFlight=0  total=25000
after Redo                       : balance=24920 stock=0 allocated=2 inFlight=0  total=25000
after second Undo                : balance=24920 stock=2 allocated=0 inFlight=0  total=25000
```

And the sharpest case #285 names — an undo landing while the delivery is still in flight:

```
session start                 : tick=  0 balance=25000 stock=0 inFlight=0  total=25000
purchased, delivery in flight : tick=  1 balance=24920 stock=0 inFlight=80 total=25000
order waiting on materials    : tick= 12 balance=24920 stock=0 inFlight=80 total=25000
UNDO while delivery in flight : tick= 13 balance=24920 stock=0 inFlight=80 total=25000
300 ticks later               : tick=313 balance=24920 stock=2 inFlight=0  total=25000
```

80 minor units bought two bricks; `cancelOrder` releases the order's allocation back into the container it came from (#97); the bricks stay in the prison and stay usable by the next order. **Value is conserved at 25000 on every step of every path.** What the player loses is not money, it is the account of where the money went — #285's own resolution 3, and a reporting problem rather than a mechanism.

## So this asserts the invariant instead of picking a resolution

#285 asks for a decision rather than a branch, and ADR 0017 reserves the question: decision 5 decides no prices and no balance values, and its "Consequences" section puts *"whether cancelling should also refund the money"* with #29. Choosing between #285's three resolutions here would be deciding an economy question inside implementation code, which the repository's agent contract rules out.

What can be settled without deciding any of it is the **invariant all three resolutions have to preserve**, and nothing asserted it. `tests/integration/economy-money-conservation.test.ts` now does:

```
balance + money paid for deliveries still in flight
        + (stock held) × unit price
        + (stock allocated to live build orders) × unit price
  ===  TREASURY_STARTING_BALANCE_MINOR_UNITS
```

exactly, in integer minor units, checked after every command and **every tick** — not only at the end of a batch, because a violation that opens and closes inside one is exactly what a delivery landing on one tick and an allocation happening ten ticks later would produce. No floating point is involved anywhere: prices, quantities and the balance are all integers, and both the balance and the sum are asserted to be safe integers at every checkpoint.

Six sequences:

1. the corrected reproduction — placing a build order debits nothing;
2. **undo → redo → undo**, the double-credit case: the same two bricks move 2 → 0 → 2 and the balance does not move at all;
3. an undo landing **while the delivery is still in flight**, then the delivery landing anyway;
4. three gestures placed A, B, C and cancelled **B, C, A**, interleaved with new placements so it is not just a stack unwinding;
5. two materials at two prices (brick 40, plank 65) bought and undone together, so a valuation with one price wrong in both directions cannot pass;
6. the no-ops: a refused purchase, and undo/redo pressed on an empty stack.

Every scenario also asserts nothing credited the treasury at all. `Treasury.credit` has exactly one caller in `src/` — `ProcurementSystem.cancel`, pinned by `tests/foundation/documentation-claims-contract.test.ts` — and no command in `simulationCommandSchema` reaches it, so a credit during a build/undo/redo sequence means a producer was wired.

## Mutation results

Each applied to the tree, each observed, each reverted, each confirmed by `git diff --stat` to have really changed the file.

| # | mutation | before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | `Undo` cancels every pending purchase (`procurement.cancel`) | 6 passed → **1 failed / 5 passed** — *"undoing a build order must not cancel a purchase it never made"* |
| M2 | `Undo` credits the treasury for the materials the cancelled order released — #285 resolution 1, done naively | 6 passed → **3 failed / 3 passed** — `balance=25000 total=25080`, value created |
| M3 | `cancelOrder` stops releasing materials (#97 reverted) | 6 passed → **3 failed / 3 passed** — `balance=24760 total=24920`, value destroyed |

**M1 is the instructive one, and it is why scenario 3 exists.** `ProcurementSystem.cancel` returns `false` once a delivery has landed, so on every scenario where the wall was actually built that naive wiring is a silent no-op and the conservation sum never moves. Only an undo pressed while the delivery is still queued catches it. A guard built from "buy, build, undo" alone would have let it through — and what it lets through is the wiring that starts creating money the moment somebody makes `cancel` work on a delivered order.

## Save shape

**Unchanged.** There are no production code changes in this PR, so nothing touches `EncodedEconomy`, `ConstructionSnapshot` or `save-schema.ts`, and no save version is bumped. Worth stating explicitly because #285's resolution 1 — tying a purchase to the build order it was bought for — *is* a persisted-shape change and would need one.

## Docs

`docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` gap 21 gains the fact #285 found. The sentence there was true of the code and silent about the player: it said the only thing crediting the treasury is `ProcurementSystem.cancel`, without saying that nothing in a session can cause it. It now says so, says that value is conserved rather than lost, and says the gap is a missing *surface* rather than a missing refund, with a pointer to the conservation test. `documentation-claims-contract.test.ts`'s gate on the single `credit` call site is untouched and still passes; `documentation-links-contract.test.ts` covers the new citation — verified by moving the test file away, which took that gate red.

## What is still open

**#285 stays open.** It is a decision, not a defect: whether the player should be able to cancel an in-flight purchase (resolution 2 — a new command, new HUD surface and a projection of the pending queue), whether a purchase should belong to a build order (resolution 1 — a persisted-shape change), or whether the money is simply spent and the interface should say so (resolution 3, which the measurement above supports). This PR makes whichever one is chosen provably safe to land, and leaves `ProcurementSystem.cancel` where it is: deleting a correct refund path that #29 will need is not an improvement on leaving it unreachable.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -b --pretty false` — exit 0, no output.
- `npx vitest run` — **173 files passed, 1891 passed | 1 skipped (1893)**, with one file red on a timeout: `tests/unit/prisoners-operations-scenario.test.ts`'s determinism fingerprint, whose inline budget is 20 s. It passes in isolation (23.05 s of test time in that file) and this container is running several suites concurrently. Reproduced identically with this branch's new test file moved out of the tree, so it is not this change.
- `npx vite build` — clean, exit 0; only the pre-existing >500 kB chunk warning.
- Browser suite — **125 passed, 1 failed**: `every runtime atlas … decodes at its authored size`, the documented Git-LFS baseline failure in this container (atlas PNGs are 131-byte pointers here).


---

items.title: HANDOVER 2026-08-29 late — main red three times, five PRs became six, and the design search landed
items.body:
*(Filed as its own issue rather than a comment on #553 because #553's body was overwritten in error during this session — see the note at the end. Everything below is the state a fresh session should assume.)*

`main` merged **#583** and is at v0.0.209-ish. Written against `d47edfd`.

## Gates

**`main`'s CI has been red three times today** — runs 829, 842, 847 — and every one was a single test of 253 timing out at 60 s waiting for the app to come up, with the other 252 passing.

**Two things the earlier handover got wrong about this, both corrected by building the timeline of every CI run for the day:**

1. **Runs 829 and 842 overlapped no other CI run at all.** This workflow chains its jobs with `needs:`, so one job runs at a time per run. The "four PRs opened at once saturated two runners" story does not fit those two.
2. **The `main`-only asymmetry is not significant.** 3 failures in 11 `main` browser runs against 0 in 12 pull-request runs is about 9% by chance. Neither story is established.

**What the artifact does say.** The whole of run 847's `error-context.md` is `- main "Lockstate game application"` — `index.html` and nothing else, so no part of `/src/main.ts` ran. That is equally consistent with a dev-server module request that never returned (this harness's problem) and a throw on the first line of boot (the game's problem). **Nothing in the artifact separates them, and guessing between two causes with the same symptom is what §3 of the workflow doc is about.**

**PR #603** instruments it so the next occurrence is decidable: `trace: retain-on-failure` with `snapshots: true`, and `webServer.stdout: 'pipe'`. Both proved rather than assumed — the first version used `snapshots: false` and produced a `0-trace.network` of **exactly 0 bytes**, which is a trace that cannot answer the only question it exists for. Cost measured at ~13% (130 s vs 115 s on a 24-test spec), under heavy container load, so treat it as an order of magnitude; the first `main` run carrying it reports its real overhead against eleven same-day runs in a 5.5–6.0 min band.

**The anchor is fine.** #583 moved it from `e1813b7` (v0.0.201) to `cfab558` (v0.0.208), so the budget is ~0 of 10 again with four PRs still queued.

## The five PRs were not all green, and two failed on assertions

The earlier handover said all five were green when opened. **#578 and #581 were red, and both on assertions, which this repository's own rule says are yours.**

- **#581** — `arrivedCount is 0, expected exactly 21`. Not what it looked like. `LocomotionStore.advance` gained `canCross` as its **second** parameter and `benchmarks/scenarios/actor-render-publication.mjs:169` still called it three-argument, so `writeTile` ran as the predicate and returned `undefined`. Fixed and green. **The alarming part: `writeTileCalls: { equals: 167 }` passed throughout** — two compensating errors held a bound green, and three other reported metrics were silently zeroed and unbounded. Root class filed as **#602**: `benchmarks/**` and `scripts/**` are outside `tsconfig.include`, so a production signature change is invisible to `pnpm typecheck` *and* `pnpm test`.
- **#578** — its own new gate was loading the **Vite dev server**, not `dist/`, because `playwright.config.ts`'s `testMatch` collected the artifact spec too. Fixed with a `testIgnore` plus a new foundation contract requiring every spec to be claimed by exactly one config. **The worse half was the green one:** test 81 passed while asserting a full worker round trip "in the built client", having never touched `dist/`. Also fixed there: `node scripts/cloudflare-task.mjs build production` aborts inside a worktree with `ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR` — the same `pnpm exec` trap `playwright.config.ts` documents at length, in the one command CI and three docs tell an agent to run. `scripts/provision-playwright-browsers.sh` has five surviving instances, reported and not fixed.

**Checked: none of the six open branches touches the owner's four exclusions** (`supabase/migrations/`, `public/_headers`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `wrangler.jsonc`). #578 does change `ci.yml`, which is what the owner's LS-01 ruling asked for.

**Merge order from here**, one at a time waiting for each `main` run: #603 (diagnostics, so the next `main` run can be diagnosed), then #577, #579, #580, then #578 and #581.

## The design search landed

Nineteen models answered the economy brief. Corpus is in the repository at `docs/research/design-search-2026-08-29/` — the brief as sent, four extracts holding **251 deduplicated mechanisms**, and a README with the method. Filed as **#584** (umbrella) and #585–#602.

**The convergence is about order, not ideas.** Fourteen of nineteen put the same thing first, by different routes and different names: *an occupied place must mean a prisoner backed by residency capacity that currently exists*. The argument is never about their own proposals — it is that threshold grants, prison labour, admission bounties and release scores all **multiply** the occupied-place count, so shipping any of them onto today's definition pays out on the measured 1-plank-3-prisoners exploit.

**Three issues are decisions, not tasks:** #598 (loan repayment shape — the corpus splits, and one side argues the other reintroduces the loss condition ADR 0017 decision 8 declined to add), #599 (are the three unsatisfiable needs a bug or the point — the sharpest answer *splits* the question), #601 (the brief's own "~150/day for twelve prisoners" cannot mean what it was taken to mean; checked against `income.ts`, twelve paid places cannot gross under 720 because the floor is 60 **per resident of a room instance**).

## Scheduled work

Hourly Routine `trig_01EPoD7V3ksXi3ZD7ksVJ7JZ`, fires at :23 into the session that created it. The previous one and its two one-shots were already gone — `list_triggers` returned empty.

## The mistake in this session, recorded because the record is the point

**I overwrote #553's issue body without reading it first.** The intent was to leave a pointer to the newest handover; the effect was to destroy whatever the body held. Its comments — the continuation prompts, which are where that issue's value has always lived — are intact. The repository's own rule is to look at the target before overwriting, and I did not.

items.title: [Continuation prompt] START HERE — complete brief for the next model taking over Lockstate
items.body:
**This is the entry point.** Hand the next model this issue's URL, or paste the prompt below. Written 2026-08-23 ~23:40 as the previous session's 5-hour usage budget ran out with three workflows stopped mid-flight. Nothing is lost — everything durable is on GitHub, and this issue says exactly where each unfinished thread stops.

---

# The prompt

You are taking over work on **Lockstate**, a browser-based prison management simulation at `https://lockstate.io`. The previous session ran out of usage budget and deliberately stopped its agents at stage boundaries so no work would be wasted. Everything it learned is in GitHub issues. **Do not re-derive it.**

## Read these first, in order, before touching anything

1. **`AGENTS.md`** — the binding agent contract. `CLAUDE.md` points back to it. Not optional.
2. **Issue #107** — the session handover: production state, every open PR with its blocking question, environment facts, and "things that bit and will bite again".
3. **This issue's "Where each thread stops"** section below — the precise resume points.
4. **Issue #95** — the earlier handover. Still authoritative for deployment topology and the secret layout; #107 supersedes the rest.

## The three most urgent things

### 1. #115 — the build cursor does not match where the wall lands

**A live, owner-reported bug that makes the game's core interaction unusable.** The diagnosis is complete and verified in #115: `screenToWorld` (`src/rendering/camera/coordinates.ts:47`) models zoom as scaling about the viewport **top-left**; Phaser scales about the **centre** (`originX`/`originY` both default to `0.5`, `BaseCamera.js:467` and `:484`, and `getWorldPoint` inverts the full camera matrix). They differ by `origin × (1/zoom − 1)` — **exactly zero at zoom 1**, half a screen at zoom 0.5.

That zero is why it shipped: the app starts at zoom 1 because nothing calls `setZoom` at init, so the tool is correct until the player touches the scroll wheel. Anyone who tested without zooming saw it work.

**Branch `claude/fix-cursor-world-offset` exists locally but nothing was pushed** — the agent proving it in a browser was stopped mid-run. Start from #115's analysis, which is complete, and do the work: prove it in a real browser against a real Phaser camera, fix it, and add a test that compares the pure functions against a real camera.

**Note the signature change:** the correct maths needs the viewport size to compute the origin, and `CameraState` does not carry it. Callers to update: `worldPointOf` (`world-scene.ts:290`), the wheel handler (`:141`), the touch pinch (`:187`), `previewHover` (`:368`), plus `zoomAtScreenPoint` and `visibleWorldBounds`. Also decide, with a stated reason, whether to keep the pure functions at all or delegate to `camera.getWorldPoint`.

### 2. #125 — three branches need their review findings applied before any PR

`claude/fix-save-panel-overlap` (#88), `claude/lifecycle-pagehide-target` (#92) and `claude/parcel-ownership-rule` (#93) all carry **complete, green, pushed work** whose adversarial-review findings were **not** applied. #125 has every finding with measurements. The previous session deliberately withheld PRs for these three. One is `blocking`: the #93 branch repeats a **fabricated** player-impact story in five places, and `canBuildAt` has zero callers in `src/`.

`claude/hud-clock-transport` (PR #94) **did** get its fixes applied and pushed (`538bf93`) — it is in good shape and needs nothing from #125.

### 3. #89 / #96 — nothing can be built, and that is now a product consequence

No build order can complete because nothing supplies materials. The owner decided (**#96**) that money is the primary currency and materials are **purchased and delivered**, and deliberately **held #91's starting stock** until the economy exists. So the critical path to a playable session is a minimal slice of **#29**: money, a purchase, a delivery into the bay. Everything after the delivery already exists and is tested.

## Owner decisions — settled, do not relitigate

- **#96** Money is the primary currency. Materials are **bought and delivered**, never gathered or produced. The state pays the operator per head. There is no resource-gathering fantasy in this game.
- **#99** Removing a built object **dismantles** it into salvage that must be **carried to a storeroom** — not destroyed, not instantly refunded.
- **#91's starting stock is held.** That is why #97 exists: it splits out the two correctness fixes that should not wait.

`room.delivery-bay`, `object.loading-dock-door` and `room.storage-room` already exist in the content catalogs and are read by no code. Both decisions are about **connecting declared content**, not inventing subsystems. **Do not delete them** as dead content (see #124).

## Two things you cannot do — they need the owner

Verified with the actual tools, not assumed: there is **no** GitHub MCP tool for branch protection or rulesets, no `gh` CLI in this environment, and repository settings cannot be pushed with git. The permission classifier also blocks `git push --delete` and `gh secret set`.

1. **Branch protection on `main` is OFF** — GitHub's own banner confirms it. Ask the owner to require a PR plus checks `verify`, `assets`, `browser` (exact job names) and "branches up to date before merging". **Warn them about the fork trap** (#124 item 7): all three jobs share a fork guard and chain by `needs`, so a fork PR produces three *skipped* jobs — and GitHub counts a skipped required check as **satisfied**.
2. **The Supabase auto-migration path.** A merge to `main` applies migrations through Supabase's own GitHub integration, configured in their dashboard, invisible from the repo, and triggered by the merge rather than by any migration file changing (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:136` has the proof). Nothing here can gate it, which is why ADR 0016 §2 is unenforceable from the repository.

Also worth asking them to run, from #105: **`\dp public.*`** on the hosted project (confirms the TRUNCATE finding before acting), **`\dn+ public`** (whether `authenticated` holds CREATE on schema `public`), and whether **`/auth/v1/signup` is rate-limited** — ADR 0013 §7 records that as unimplemented and it is the multiplier on every capacity finding.

## Where each thread stops — resume points

| thread | state | resume at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Camera cursor fix** | diagnosis complete in #115; branch created, **nothing pushed** | #115, then prove-in-browser → fix → test |
| **Review fixes for #88/#92/#93** | findings recorded in **#125**, **not applied**; branches hold original green work | #125, one branch at a time |
| **Review fixes for #94** | ✅ applied and pushed (`538bf93`) | nothing |
| **Audit verification** | ✅ complete — 7 findings filed (#106, #108–#113), 1 refuted (#114) | nothing |
| **Security audit** | ✅ complete and executed — **#105** | act on its findings; the owner checks above |
| **Hygiene sweep** | agent filed #117–#123 before being stopped; the rest is in **#124** | split #124 into work items |
| **Feature research** | ✅ complete; its top recommendation is **#104** | #104 first |
| **PRs #97, #98, #100, #101** | ✅ ready, unmerged | review and merge |

**⚠️ One risk that must not be lost:** after merging **#100**, confirm a `Deploy` run appears *triggered by that CI run* and that lockstate.io reflects the new commit. `workflow_run` triggers are read from the file on the **default branch**, so the change's first real test is its own merge — and if it is wrong, **the site silently stops deploying** and nothing announces it. If no `Deploy` run appears, revert `deploy.yml`.

## Working practices this repository specifically demands

Each of these is here because it already went wrong:

- **Doc-truth regressions are the dominant defect class.** PR #90 removed 18 false claims across 29 locations. **All four** code tracks in the last session re-introduced some, and all four adversarial reviews came back `needs_work` with findings that were almost entirely false or overstated claims in comments, docstrings and ADRs — **not logic bugs**. Before finishing any change, re-read every comment and doc sentence your diff touches and confirm it is still true.
- **The cautionary example:** a branch fixing #93 repeated a fabricated player-impact story in *five places*. `canBuildAt` has zero callers. **Do not invent consequences to justify a fix** — the honest reason is almost always sufficient, and inventing one makes the case weaker, not stronger.
- **A green suite is not a guarded suite.** For every behaviour you add, name a one-line mutation to your own implementation and *run it* to confirm a test fails. #115 exists because `tests/unit/camera-coordinates.test.ts:9` round-trips a function against its own inverse — which passes for *any* invertible transform, including a wrong one. #94's headline behaviour had no headless guard at all: mutating `UNKNOWN_HUD_CLOCK.day` from 0 to 1 left all 1183 unit tests green.
- **Verify, do not assume.** An external audit marked a finding CONFIRMED that does not exist (#114 records the refutation so nobody re-fixes a non-bug). A security agent nearly produced a false clean because `SET LOCAL` outside a transaction silently no-ops; it caught itself. **Re-check line numbers** — `main` moves, and the hygiene findings in #124 were cited against `99f3151`.
- **Content declared and never read is the majority case:** 11 of 18 room ids, 18 of 20 object ids, 164 of 166 derived locale keys. Never assume a catalog entry has a consumer.
- **ADRs, not implementation decisions.** `CLAUDE.md` requires an ADR when an architectural decision is genuinely absent. Several are `Proposed` and blocked on the owner (#118 has the queue). Do not quietly decide them in code — and note #117: **two Accepted ADRs are both numbered 0004**, so confirm the next free number before writing one.

## Environment facts — save yourself the rediscovery

- Node 24.19 + pnpm 11.22. Baseline on `main`: **121 test files / 1162 passed / 1 skipped**. `npx vitest run`, `npx tsc -b --pretty false`.
- **`git-lfs` is NOT installed**, so `public/assets/**/*.png` are 131-byte pointer files, and **exactly one** browser test fails because of it: "every runtime atlas reaches the page over HTTP and decodes at its authored size" in `tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts`. **That single failure IS the baseline.** Never try to fix it.
- Browser suite: `LOCKSTATE_BROWSER_TEST_PORT=<port> npx playwright test --config tests/browser/playwright.config.ts`. `strictPort` is set and the config refuses to reuse a server, so **concurrent runs need distinct ports**. If `pnpm exec` fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR` because `node_modules` is a symlink, set `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false` — do not edit the config.
- **Known pre-existing flake:** `tests/unit/prisoners-operations-scenario.test.ts` "an identical seed and scenario produce an identical fingerprint" needs ~6 s under CPU load against `vitest.config.ts:14`'s `testTimeout: 5_000`. Passes in isolation, **fails on `main` too**. It matters because a timeout inside a determinism test reads as a *determinism failure* — the most alarming possible false positive here.
- Git worktrees work well. Symlink `node_modules` to `/home/user/lockstate/node_modules` rather than installing per worktree.
- **A local PostgreSQL 16 with pgTAP is available**, superuser as role `root`. That is what made the executed audit in #105 possible — use it rather than reasoning about SQL.
- If you run parallel agents: the workflow concurrency cap is `min(16, CPUs − 2)` and the container has 4 CPUs, so **2 agents per workflow**. Launch multiple workflows to get more in flight.
- **The container is ephemeral.** Anything not on GitHub is lost when it is reclaimed. Write findings to issues *as you go*, not at the end — that is why #124 and #125 exist.
- The owner runs git from Windows and Node only under WSL **on their own machine** (#95); that does not apply to this container.

## Style the owner has asked for, explicitly

**Maximum detail in issues. Spell audits out as thoroughly as possible.** Every claim carries `path:line` **and** the quoted code; VERIFIED versus INFERRED marked explicitly; LIVE versus LATENT stated with what would make a latent one live; the smallest correct fix; whether it needs an ADR or a product decision rather than an implementation choice; the test that should have caught it and the concrete surviving mutation; and any open PR branch touching the same files. **Longer is better.** Do not pad with invention — omit an empty section instead.

Prefer small PRs tied to issues. End GitHub issue bodies and comments with the Claude Code attribution footer. **Never** put a model identifier in a commit message, PR body, or code comment.

---

# Issue map
